  • It changed a setting: the lower layer's value applies. Skip datacenters/dc2.yaml on nonprod-west-1 and the registry allowlist reverts to the element defaults, so pulls from mirror.dc2.example.com fail.

The validator, which CI runs on every pull request in your repository, catches most causes (Validator rules):

Cause Validator Typo in a valueFiles entry POLICY050 Entry for a file the cluster's pinned revision lacks POLICY052 values/clusters/ file no fleet file reads, such as a misnamed one POLICY052 (warning: reported on the pull request, doesn't fail it; Reading the output)

To check by hand, compare the files the Application lists with the files at the cluster's revision. Any listed ../../values/<path> with no matching values/<path> in the second output was skipped:

oc get applications.argoproj.io infra-nodes-prod-east-1 -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.source.helm.valueFiles}'
git fetch origin
git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- values/   # the fleet file's revision: branch, tag or SHA

items.title: Merge rules
items.text:
Helm merges the files in order:

  • Scalars: the last file that sets the key wins.
  • Maps: merge key by key, so a layer sets only what changes.
  • Lists: replace whole. A layer can't append to a list; it restates every item it keeps.
  • Removing: a higher layer can't take back a key a lower layer set. null doesn't restore the element default: the converter sees no value (Helm 3.17 and later keep the null under stack, earlier versions delete the key). To drop a policies, templates or operatorPolicies entry, set enabled: false. To drop a config map entry, such as a MetalLB pool, move it out of the shared layer into the cluster files that need it.

That is why collections a layer must extend are maps keyed by name: policies, templates, operatorPolicies, and element settings such as MetalLB's ipAddressPools or team-gitops' teams.

Map: set only what changesList: restate everything 
# values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml
stack:
  userMonitoring:
    config:
      prometheus:
        retention: 72h   # other prometheus keys keep their defaults
        storage: 20Gi

# values/datacenters/dc2.yaml
stack:
  remediations:
    config:
      allowedRegistries:
        - mirror.dc2.example.com:8443
        - quay.io                    # the defaults, restated
        - registry.redhat.io
        - image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000

Common changes, each settable from any layer:

Change Key An element on or off stack.remediations.enabled. Off unless true A policy on or off stack.remediations.policies.registries.enabled. On unless false A template on or off stack.gitops.policies.link.templates.argocd-console.enabled. On unless false An operator on or off stack.metallb.operatorPolicies.metallb.enabled. false stops managing it; it stays installed (Removal and pruning) One element in inform stack.infraNodes.default.remediationAction: inform. Every policy of the element that sets no action of its own One policy in inform stack.infraNodes.policies.mcp.remediationAction: inform. Beats the element's default Everything in inform global.remediationAction: inform (Global keys) A converter setting stack.<el>.config.<key>, or policies.<p>.templates.<t>.config.<key> for one template only. The template's config is merged over the element's (How an element is built). Keys and defaults are in the element's values.yaml and README One operator field stack.metallb.operatorPolicies.metallb.versions. versions is a list and replaces (Operator versions)

Use false to turn a piece off, never null: null counts as unset, which turns a policy on and an element off (What renders).

items.title: Schema
items.text:
Helm merges every layer first, then validates the result once against policy-library's values.schema.json, which covers the stack key and global (Helm passes top-level global to every subchart, the library included). A misspelled or mistyped library key fails the render. The wording depends on the Helm version:

Helm 3.18.4 and earlier (OpenShift GitOps 1.18, CI)Helm 3.18.5 and later 
Error: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
stack:
- certManager: Additional property enabeld is not allowed

Error: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
stack:
- at '/certManager': additional properties 'enabeld' not allowed

Argo CD shows the Application as ComparisonError and neither syncs nor prunes, so the hub keeps the Policies it had (When an Application fails). Every element, and lifecycle/, validates the whole stack key, so one typo in a shared layer fails every Application that reads it.

Never set skipSchemaValidation on the ApplicationSet

The schema is the only render-time check that rejects unknown library keys such as enabeld. Without it enabeld: false merges silently and does nothing, and a policy you meant to turn off keeps enforcing. A loud ComparisonError that changes nothing on the hub is the safer failure.

Both checks run before merge. The validator renders every element on the pull request, so a schema failure fails CI (RENDER000, and POLICY035 at the layer that set the key). Argo CD runs the schema again at sync.

The schema checks library keys only. POLICY035 also checks every .yaml file under values/ and the root values.yaml, used by a fleet file or not. Name layers .yaml: Argo CD reads a listed .yml file, but POLICY035 skips it.

Mistake Caught by Unknown key in an element (stack.certManager.enabeld) schema, POLICY035 Wrong type for a library key (enabled: "yes") schema global.remediationAction: enforce schema Unknown top-level or global key POLICY035 Unknown element (stack.certManagr) POLICY035 global nested under stack (stack.global.remediationAction): ignored by the render POLICY035 policies key that names no policy of the element render, POLICY035 templates key that names no template and sets no file render, POLICY035 operatorPolicies key that names no operator of the element render, POLICY032 Top-level config key absent from the element's values.yaml POLICY035 Deeper config keys, and the type of any config value nothing: replicas: three renders and fails later, in the converter or when ACM applies the object

The render errors name the fix, for example policy-library: policies.mcp.templates.ghost has no file - add converters/mcp/ghost.yaml or set file (Names that don't exist).

items.title: Global keys
items.text:
global is a top-level key that policy-library reads for every element and for lifecycle/. One setting changes every Policy of every element, on the clusters that read the layer. Set it in a cluster file for one cluster, or in a shared layer for a site or an environment. Under stack it is ignored.

Key Effect remediationAction inform sets every Policy to report instead of enforce, lifecycle Policies included, overriding the element and policy settings (Dry run). enforce is rejected by the schema: it would also enforce templates built only to report, such as readiness checks. To undo a shared layer's inform for one cluster, set remediationAction: "" in its cluster file; each Policy's own action applies again. catalogSources Maps an operator's CatalogSource name to its replacement, for every operator of every element (Disconnected clusters) 
global:
  remediationAction: inform
  catalogSources:
    redhat-operators: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20

items.title: Example files
items.text:
Upstream's values/ holds examples for the example clusters in the docs, and the layers the validator's test fleet files in tools/validator/testdata/clusters/ read. copier copies neither into your repository, so your values/ starts empty. Copy an example by hand if it fits, and read it first.

The examples enforce

Listing a layer applies it on the next sync, and the elements it turns on enforce, so a cluster that lists a copy of environments/prod.yaml changes at once. Start a new cluster with an empty valueFiles, or set global.remediationAction: inform in its cluster file first.

What each example file holds File Holds environments/prod.yaml Prod baseline: cert-manager, External Secrets, Compliance Operator, remediations (samples on, registry allowlist off), DNS environments/nonprod.yaml Nothing datacenters/dc1.yaml install.baseDomain only, so nothing for an imported cluster datacenters/dc2.yaml Registry allowlist through the dc2 mirror. Applies only where a cluster enables remediations platforms/aws.yaml Node policies: clone the worker MachineSet. install: Hive platforms/vmware.yaml Node policies: clone each MachineSet per failure domain. install: Hive platforms/baremetal.yaml Node policies: no MachineSets, label nodes. install: SiteConfig platforms/kubevirt.yaml install only: KubeVirt, 2-node workers pool platforms/agent.yaml install only: Agent, no default NodePool tenants/payments.yaml GitOps operator plus a payments team Argo CD acm/acm-dc1.yaml Hub ACM and GitOps, commented out (why) clusters/acm-dc1.yaml Hub elements, and which are off and why (cim for SiteConfig clusters) clusters/prod-east-1.yaml Infra nodes, machine health, user monitoring clusters/hcp-agent.yaml install: hosted control plane service publishing. stack: guest MetalLB pool clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml Registry enforcement, MetalLB pool, user monitoring clusters/aws-prod.yaml ODF to Loki chain. Rename to the real ManagedCluster name first

tenants/payments.yaml and clusters/aws-prod.yaml are only key-checked (POLICY035) until a fleet file lists them. Render errors in them show up on that pull request.

items.title: Writing an element
items.text:
Read How an element is built first: folders under converters/ create Policies and templates, and values.yaml only configures them. ACM terms (Policy, ConfigurationPolicy, OperatorPolicy, musthave, inform/enforce) are explained in ACM policies in brief.

Every key the library reads is in the policy-library README.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
Need For Without it pip install -r tools/requirements.txt (PyYAML) create-element.sh and tools/doc-generator.py The script creates stack/<name>/, then stops with README not generated: .... Run the generator it names; don't rerun the script, which refuses an existing directory mise install, then mise activate (Setup) The Go, Helm and prek versions pinned in mise.toml. The validator and hooks need them make -C tools/validator can't find go, or renders with a different Helm than Argo CD prek install (optional) Runs the repo hooks, including element-readmes, on each commit A stale README fails CI instead of your commit A nonprod cluster in your fleet. Its fleet file, fleet/<cluster>.yaml, says which Git revision and values layers it gets (Fleet files) Steps 10-12 You can't try the element on a cluster. Stop after step 9 and rely on CI

policy-library lives in this repo, in lib/policy-library. Your Chart.yaml declares it with repository: file://../../lib/policy-library and a floor such as version: "^4.0.0", which create-element.sh copies from the sample. Helm packages it into stack/<name>/charts/ (gitignored) on every preview and validate, and Argo CD does the same when it renders. If your element needs a library feature added in 4.N, raise the floor to ^4.N.0 (Library changes).

items.title: Workflow
items.text:
1. Scaffold.

    tools/create-element.sh demo "Demo element"

    Copies the sample element to stack/demo/, renames my-element to demo and myElement to its camelCase values key, and generates the README. It refuses a name that isn't kebab-case, is over 17 characters or collides with another element (POLICY091); see Naming for why.

    In upstream PolicyStack (where .release-please/ exists) it also adds copier's answers template, so adopters can copy the element from the next release (Releases). In your own repository it doesn't: the element is local, and copier never touches it. Either way the element starts as policystk.io/stability: preview (Versions and deprecation).

    The copy is a working example: operator demo points at package demo-operator, which doesn't exist, and converters/install/demo-instance.yaml is a sample ConfigMap. Replace or delete both in steps 2 and 3.

  2. Write converters. A converter is one file, converters/<policy>/<template>.yaml. Each directory becomes a Policy, each file in it a ConfigurationPolicy named <policy>-<template> (rendered names). Put the manifests you want on the cluster in it, several separated by --- if needed (Converter shapes). converters/install/demo-instance.yaml renders as:

    Policy install-demo-<cluster> (excerpt)
    kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: install-demo-<cluster>          # Policy install of release demo-<cluster>
spec:
  policy-templates:
    - objectDefinition:
        kind: ConfigurationPolicy
        metadata:
          name: install-demo-instance
        spec:
          object-templates:
            - complianceType: musthave      # the fields you list must match; others are left alone
              objectDefinition:
                apiVersion: v1
                kind: ConfigMap
                ...                         # your file, as written

    Pasting oc get -o yaml output

    Strip status and every server-set metadata field: uid, resourceVersion, generation, creationTimestamp, managedFields, ownerReferences and the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation. ACM compares every field you list, and it can't set status or server-set fields, so a copied one keeps the template NonCompliant forever or ties it to one instance of the object.

    .yml files, files directly under converters/ and names starting with _ are not discovered (partials). POLICY021 warns when nothing renders one.

  3. Declare operators. Operators need no converter. Set namespace, subscription.name, subscription.channel and displayName under operatorPolicies.<key>. The library adds three templates to Policy install: install-<key>-ns (the Namespace), install-<key> (the OperatorPolicy, which creates the OperatorGroup and Subscription) and install-<key>-status (an inform check for a CSV with that displayName in phase Succeeded). Find the values on a cluster:

    oc get packagemanifests -n openshift-marketplace \
  -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,SOURCE:.status.catalogSource,DEFAULT:.status.defaultChannel | grep -i <product>
# NAME is subscription.name, SOURCE subscription.source, DEFAULT the channel most clusters want
oc get packagemanifest <package> -n openshift-marketplace \
  -o jsonpath='{range .status.channels[*]}{.name}: {.currentCSVDesc.displayName} {.currentCSVDesc.installModes[?(@.supported==true)].type}{"\n"}{end}'
# per channel: displayName, then the supported install modes

    A wrong displayName never goes green

    It defaults to subscription.name, which is rarely the display name. The status check then never matches: it stays NonCompliant, and every template that waits for the operator stays Pending, which ignorePending shows as Compliant. You see install-<key>-status NonCompliant on the hub while oc get csv -n <namespace> on the cluster shows the operator Succeeded. Compare that CSV's spec.displayName with yours.

    Without operatorGroup.targetNamespaces the OperatorGroup watches all namespaces. An operator whose install modes lack AllNamespaces fails to install that way: set targetNamespaces: [<namespace>] (stack/compliance). Installing into openshift-operators? Set operatorGroup.name: global-operators to reuse the existing one, because a second OperatorGroup in a namespace breaks OLM.

    No operator? Delete both operatorPolicies and the sample's waitForOperator. Deleting only operatorPolicies fails the render: waitForOperator "demo" on policy "install" matches no enabled entry in operatorPolicies.

  4. Put configuration that needs the operator in its own Policy. A CR, or anything in a namespace or CRD the operator creates, goes in its own Policy that depends on install, with waitForOperator on the template that needs the CRD (waiting and ordering). Policy install then means "operator installed", which other elements can wait on, and a layer can turn the configuration off without unmanaging the operator. The sample keeps its ConfigMap in install with waitForOperator only to stay one Policy; that works too. From stack/metallb/values.yaml:

    policies:
  config:
    dependencies:
      - name: install           # Policy config-metallb-<cluster> stays Pending until install is Compliant
    templates:
      metallb-instance:
        waitForOperator: metallb  # this template waits for install-metallb-status

  5. Move site data into config. Site data is anything that differs between clusters or environments. Converters read it as .Config (merge rules). Expose curated settings, a named key with a working default, and build the manifest in the converter. The sample does this with logLevel: config.logLevel: info in values.yaml, logLevel: {{ .Config.logLevel | quote }} in the converter. A layer then sets logLevel: debug instead of copying a CR spec. Nothing checks a setting's type. A map of name to spec is fine when the object is nothing but site data (stack/metallb ipAddressPools).

    config in the element's values.yaml is the contract:

    • Every top-level key a converter reads must be declared there, under the element's config or the config of each template that renders the converter (stack/compliance declares severity only per template). An undeclared key renders as null, and POLICY022 fails the PR.
    • A layer may only set declared top-level keys of the element's config. POLICY035 fails a typo that would otherwise do nothing. Keys below the top level are not checked.
    • The comment above each key becomes its row in the README.

  6. Preview.

    make -C tools/validator preview ELEMENT=demo CLUSTER=nonprod-west-1

    Turns the element on and prints demo.yaml, the Policies after Helm, and demo.evaluated.yaml, the objects ACM would apply after resolving ACM templates on an empty cluster.

    • CLUSTER names a fixture, a made-up fleet file in tools/validator/testdata/clusters/. In your repository, which has no fixtures, it names one of your fleet files instead. Without CLUSTER every fixture renders and only the file paths print. Output goes to a new temporary directory, which is left in place; PREVIEW=<dir> (relative to tools/validator) writes it there instead.
    • Only stack.demo.enabled: true is forced, so pieces shipped enabled: false stay off. To see one, turn it on temporarily in values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml, which the fixture reads.

    What the two files show and their limits: Preview.

    Step 7 is upstream only

    copier leaves the fixtures and tools/validator/testdata/inputs.yaml out of your repository, so there preview renders your fleet files and there is no all-on run. Go from step 6 to step 8.

  7. Give the all-on run its inputs. Fixtures leave a new element off, so CI renders it only in the all-on run, which turns it and every entry it ships enabled: false on by itself (Profiles). If one of those entries ranges over a config map, add a sample entry for it to tools/validator/testdata/inputs.yaml under the element's values key: an empty map fails POLICY082 (Converter shapes). Settings that conflict with the all-on run go in tools/validator/testdata/profiles/variants.yaml.

    tools/validator/testdata/inputs.yaml
    stack:
  demo:               # the values key: cert-manager would be certManager
    config:
      hosts: {example: {address: 10.0.0.1}}

  8. Validate.

    make -C tools/validator validate ELEMENT=demo

    Runs every rule on this element. Repo-wide rules such as POLICY091 still read every element. Each finding names the rule, element and source line; Reading the output explains them.

  9. Regenerate the README after any change to Chart.yaml, values.yaml or converters/:

    python tools/doc-generator.py --element demo

    With prek install, the element-readmes hook rewrites a stale README and fails the commit; git add it and commit again. CI fails on a stale README (Element reference).

  10. Pin a cluster to your branch. On feature/demo, turn the element on in the cluster's own layer:

    values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml
    stack:
  demo:
    enabled: true

    Push feature/demo to the repository Argo CD reads; a branch in a personal fork doesn't resolve. Then, from a separate branch, open a PR to the default branch that changes only the cluster's fleet file, and merge it:

    fleet/nonprod-west-1.yaml
    revision: feature/demo

    Fleet files are read only from the default branch, so an open PR changes nothing, and the same change on feature/demo would merge the element with it. Everything else, stack/ and values/ included, now comes from feature/demo for this cluster: the element and any other difference between its old revision and your branch. The PR's Render Diff comment shows exactly that (Promoting and rolling back). Each push to the branch reaches the cluster within minutes.

  11. Read the result on the hub with oc get policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n nonprod-west-1; the element's Policies are pstack.<policy>-demo-nonprod-west-1 (Compliance states). No demo Policies a few minutes after the merge means the render failed: oc get application demo-nonprod-west-1 -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}' shows the ComparisonError.

    The element starts in inform, which changes nothing on the cluster, so new config never reads Compliant there:

    • Objects that don't exist yet are NonCompliant. Inform creates nothing and approves no operator install.
    • Templates that wait for the operator are Pending, and ignorePending reports them as Compliant. That green means "not checked yet".

  12. Choose the default action and un-pin. Check that every violation is one you expect, then pick how the element ships. default.remediationAction: enforce in its values.yaml changes every cluster that enables it at once; inform leaves each layer to opt in with stack.demo.default.remediationAction: enforce.

    Once everything is Compliant, update feature/demo from the default branch and, in the element's PR, set revision in fleet/nonprod-west-1.yaml back to the default branch. The merge then un-pins the cluster in the same commit (POLICY052 checks a pin to the base branch against the merge commit), so it doesn't matter if GitHub deletes the branch on merge. Never delete a branch while a fleet file pins it: policystack stops generating for every cluster on that hub (When a revision breaks).

items.title: Sample element
items.text:
The tabs show the live files in tools/sample-element/, so they always match the repo: one operator, one converter reading .Config, one optional template. create-element.sh renames my-element to your name and myElement to your values key. README.md is generated.

values.yamlconverters/install/my-element-instance.yamlconverters/install/my-element-netpol.yamlChart.yaml 
stack:
  myElement:
    enabled: false

    default:
      remediationAction: inform
      severity: medium

    # Settings the converters read as `.Config`.
    config:
      # Log level the operator reads from its ConfigMap
      logLevel: info

    policies:
      install:
        description: "Install and configure the example operator"
        templates:
          my-element-instance:
            description: "Operator configuration"
            waitForOperator: my-element
          my-element-netpol:
            enabled: false
            description: "Allow ingress from the same namespace only"

    operatorPolicies:
      my-element:
        displayName: "Example Operator"
        namespace: my-element
        subscription:
          name: my-element-operator
          channel: stable
        # Allowed CSV names, pinned per layer; empty follows the channel
        versions: []

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: my-element
  namespace: my-element
data:
  logLevel: {{ .Config.logLevel | quote }}

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: same-namespace
  namespace: my-element
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector: {}

apiVersion: v2
name: my-element
description: Teaching example that tools/create-element.sh copies.
type: application
version: 0.1.0
annotations:
  policystk.io/stability: preview
dependencies:
  - name: policy-library
    alias: stack
    version: "^4.0.0"
    repository: "file://../../lib/policy-library"
  • Chart.yaml and templates/policy.yaml: leave them as they are (Anatomy). Named templates several converters share go in templates/_helpers.tpl; converters can include them (stack/compliance compliance.waivedRules).
  • versions: [] follows the channel. Pin per environment in layers (Operator versions).

items.title: What you leave out
items.text:
Write a key only when its default is wrong for your element. An arrow means "the first one set wins, left to right". Template means policies.<p>.templates.<t>, operator means operatorPolicies.<k>.

Key Resolves to enabled on the element off unless true. Elements ship false; a layer turns them on enabled on a policy, template or operator on policies one Policy per converters/ directory, plus install when there are operators policies.<p>.templates one template per converters/<p>/*.yaml remediationAction policies.<p> → default → inform. global.remediationAction: inform overrides it (Dry run) severity template or operator → policies.<p> → default → low categories, controls, standards policies.<p> → default → none template complianceType musthave (fields you list must match; all three). mustonlyhave also removes fields you don't list; mustnothave deletes the object under enforce template or operator ignorePending false; true when waitForOperator is set, so a template waiting on the operator counts as Compliant operator subscription.source, subscription.sourceNamespace redhat-operators, openshift-marketplace operator upgradeApproval Automatic operator operatorGroup.name subscription.name, watching all namespaces operator displayName subscription.name

Template remediationAction accepts only InformOnly

It keeps one template reporting inside an enforce Policy (inform, enforce and InformOnly). Set it on every template that only reports: readiness checks and mustnothave signals. Any other value fails the render: remediationAction must be one of the following: "InformOnly", "", null.

items.title: Converter shapes
items.text:
The library runs each converter through Helm with the usual .Values, .Release and .Files, plus .Config. It then looks at the trimmed output, not your source, to pick the ConfigurationPolicy field:

One objectDocumentsRaw list 
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: my-element
  namespace: my-element
data:
  logLevel: {{ .Config.logLevel | quote }}

Renders one object-templates entry: complianceType: musthave and this ConfigMap as its objectDefinition.

One object-templates entry per --- document. Empty documents are dropped. With config.maps: {a: {k: "1"}, b: {k: "2"}} this renders two entries, ConfigMaps a and b:

{{- range $name, $data := .Config.maps }}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: {{ $name }}
  namespace: my-element
data: {{- toYaml $data | nindent 2 }}
{{- end }}

Helm consumes the {{- range action, so the output starts with ---, not -, and this is not raw. Put --- first inside a range or if, and between objects elsewhere. The template's complianceType, metadataComplianceType, recordDiff, recreateOption and objectSelector apply to every document: set them on policies.<p>.templates.<t>, as stack/metallb does with complianceType: mustonlyhave. A Helm range or if is never a reason for a raw list.

Note

A --- must start the line and stand alone to separate documents. A leading --- and full-line # comments are fine. --- # c is not a separator: at the top of the file it makes the output start with -, so it is treated as raw; between objects it stays inside the previous document and the render fails with a YAML parse error. Put the comment on its own line.

Output starting with -, [ or {{ goes verbatim into object-templates-raw, a string ACM evaluates on the managed cluster as a whole. Use it only when:

  • the cluster decides how many objects there are (an ACM range over a lookup),
  • the cluster decides whether an object exists and the condition takes more than a line. A short condition is skipObject inside one of the object's fields (stack/acs/converters/central/console.yaml),
  • the cluster decides whether a field exists (an ACM if around a key, stack/cim/converters/hub/cim-provisioning.yaml),
  • several ACM statements compute a number or boolean (podsPerCore in the kubelet converters). A block scalar always yields a string, so the logic can't move into the field,
  • one object must not apply unless another's lookups succeed, or ACM variables are shared between objects. With documents, ACM resolves each object on its own and a failed object doesn't stop the others,
  • objects in one template need different complianceType or other entry options.

Say which in the converter's header comment. In practice a leading {{ after Helm comes from an escaped ACM template (Helm templates and ACM templates):

{{ "{{-" }} range (lookup "v1" "Namespace" "" "" "team=a").items {{ "}}" }}
- complianceType: musthave
  objectDefinition:
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: ConfigMap
    metadata:
      name: my-element
      namespace: {{ "{{" }} .metadata.name {{ "}}" }}
{{ "{{-" }} end {{ "}}" }}

Renders object-templates-raw: | followed by this block with the escapes removed ({{- range (lookup ... on the first line). You write each complianceType yourself, so the template's complianceType, metadataComplianceType, recordDiff, recreateOption and objectSelector don't apply. A raw list must be the template's only output; next to another document, or in a file list, it fails with renders a raw object list next to other documents. disableTemplating on a raw list fails with sets disableTemplating but renders a raw object list: ACM never parses object-templates-raw with templates disabled, so the template would apply nothing.

Output that is empty renders object-templates-raw as the string [] (an empty raw list). ACM reports a ConfigurationPolicy with no objects as Compliant without checking anything, so a Policy whose templates are all empty fails POLICY082. The usual cause is a converter ranging over a config map whose default is {} (stack/metallb ipAddressPools): give the map an entry wherever the template is enabled, and in the test profile (step 7).

items.title: Escaping
items.text:
Every ACM {{ }} in a converter is escaped from Helm as {{ "{{" }} ... {{ "}}" }}; why, and the errors an unescaped one gives, are in Helm templates and ACM templates. To use a setting inside an ACM expression, leave that part unescaped so Helm fills it in first: '{{ "{{" }} lookup "v1" "ConfigMap" "{{ .Config.namespace }}" "x" {{ "}}" }}' reaches ACM as {{ lookup "v1" "ConfigMap" "my-ns" "x" }}. Escaped, ACM receives .Config, which it doesn't have, and POLICY081 fails. make preview shows both stages: <element>.yaml after Helm, .evaluated.yaml after ACM.

ACM logic that feeds one value goes inside that value, so the object stays a document. A short expression is one quoted action, as in stack/user-monitoring/converters/ready/statefulsets.yaml. Longer logic goes in a block scalar as {{- lines, ending with one action without the dash that prints the value (stack/user-monitoring/converters/config/enable.yaml):

data:
  config.yaml: |
    {{ "{{" }}- $cm := lookup "v1" "ConfigMap" "openshift-monitoring" "cluster-monitoring-config" {{ "}}" }}
    {{ "{{" }}- $existing := index ($cm.data | default dict) "config.yaml" | default "" | fromYaml | default dict {{ "}}" }}
    {{ "{{" }} set $existing "enableUserWorkload" true | toYaml | autoindent {{ "}}" }}

Each {{- removes the line break before it, so the value holds only the last action's output. The result is always a string. A number or boolean needs one quoted action ending in | toInt or | toBool, which ACM unquotes; if that doesn't fit on a line, keep the raw list.

items.title: Partials and file reuse
items.text:
When and why to share a converter is in Partials and reuse. To do it:

  1. Name the shared file or its directory with a leading _ (converters/findings/_findings.yaml, converters/_shared/), so discovery doesn't turn it into a template or Policy of its own.
  2. Point each template at it with templates.<t>.file: the path under converters/ without .yaml (file: findings/_findings), or a list whose objects are concatenated (file: [_shared/acs-namespace, secured/tls]). Give each template its own config if the partial should render differently.
  3. Preview. A path that doesn't exist fails with converters/<path>.yaml, a file of <p>-<t>, is missing or empty. A raw converter can't be in a list (Converter shapes).

file also replaces a discovered converters/<p>/<t>.yaml; POLICY021 then warns that the file is unused.

items.title: Optional pieces
items.text:
Ship a policy, template or operator with enabled: false for things only some clusters want. A layer turns it on with its full path:

values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml
stack:
  demo:
    policies:
      install:
        templates:
          demo-netpol:
            enabled: true

The README lists it under Optional pieces with that path. Give every input it reads a working default in config. A config map with no sensible default stays {}: say in its comment that the layer turning the piece on must fill it, or CI fails POLICY082 for that cluster (Converter shapes).

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
Values live in Git, so secrets don't. A converter reads them on the hub at runtime with a hub template, {{hub ... hub}} (Hub and managed-cluster templates). The propagator re-resolves it when the Secret changes, so a rotation reaches clusters without a commit. stack/acs/converters/secured/tls.yaml:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: '{{ "{{" }}hub if eq (index .ManagedClusterLabels "local-cluster") "true" hub{{ "}}" }}{{ "{{" }} skipObject {{ "}}" }}{{ "{{" }}hub end hub{{ "}}" }}cluster-registration-secret'
  namespace: stackrox
type: Opaque
data: '{{ "{{" }}hub copySecretData "stackrox" "cluster-registration-secret" hub{{ "}}" }}'

The name line skips the object on the hub itself (label local-cluster: "true"): there the hub template emits {{ skipObject }}, which the cluster then runs, because the source Secret already lives on the hub and copying it onto itself would overwrite it.

  • copySecretData copies every key of the hub Secret's data, not its type, labels or annotations.
  • fromSecret <ns> <name> <key> returns one key's base64 value, so it belongs under data. A missing key returns ''; a missing Secret is a template error.

  • By default hub templates may only read the policy namespace (pstack). stack/acs reads stackrox, so its Policy runs them as a ServiceAccount:

    policies:
  secured:
    hubTemplateOptions:
      serviceAccountName: acs-hub-templates

    You create that ServiceAccount in pstack and give it read access to exactly what the templates read. ACS does it in its central Policy, which ships enabled: false and is turned on only in the hub's layer (values/acm/<hub>.yaml), so it runs on the hub where pstack is. Its hub-access template (stack/acs/converters/central/hub-access.yaml) grants get/list/watch on the one Secret and Route, plus ManagedClusters for .ManagedClusterLabels. Without serviceAccountName the propagator refuses the lookup and POLICY081 fails; without the RBAC the hub denies it.

items.title: Naming
items.text:
Element, policy and template names end up in every object name, and ACM caps names at 63 characters (Naming limits).

  • Lowercase kebab-case, directory name equal to the chart name (why). The values key is its camelCase (cert-manager → certManager).
  • At most 17 characters. pstack.install-<element>-<cluster> must fit 63 with a 30-character cluster name. Policy name and element name together are at most 24 characters, not counting the hyphens (ingress-cert + cert-manager = 24), so pstack.<policy>-<element>- leaves 30 for the cluster.
  • Not <another element>-..., and no other element <yours>-.... gitops on cluster dev-c and gitops-dev on cluster c would both be release gitops-dev-c (POLICY091). lifecycle is taken: the lifecycle/ chart's releases are lifecycle-<cluster>.
  • Distinctive template names. <policy>-<template> must be unique on a cluster across all elements (why). In shared Policy names (config, ready, install) name templates after the product (metallb-instance, not instance). Operator keys count: they render install-<key>.
  • No openshift- prefix or -operator suffix. An element names the product, and both spend the 17-character budget for nothing.

Renaming recreates Policies

Renaming an element or policy deletes its Policies on every cluster and creates new ones; renaming a template replaces its ConfigurationPolicy inside the same Policy. Either way, objects on the cluster stay unless the template sets pruneObjectBehavior (Removal and pruning).

items.title: Good practices
items.text:
• One product per element. Clusters turn an element on as a unit.
  • categories, controls, standards only for controls the element implements. The library adds none, and the Governance dashboard reports what you claim (annotations).
  • pruneObjectBehavior in its own commit, before any removal, because landed together the cluster never sees prune and deletes nothing. Never on a template with dependencies (POLICY033, why).

items.title: Versions and deprecation
items.text:
Upstream elements have no version of their own. Each release tag vX.Y.Z holds the framework and every element, and an adopter's answers file records the tag an element was copied from (Releases). Chart.yaml version stays 0.1.0: Argo CD renders elements from a Git path and never packages them, and nothing reads an element's own version (policy-library reads only its own).

How far an element can be relied on is its stability, stable or preview, a Chart.yaml annotation that the generated README shows. What each value promises and which elements are stable: Element stability.

stack/odf/Chart.yaml
annotations:
  policystk.io/stability: preview

create-element.sh writes preview. Any other value fails the README generator. In your repository, an element you wrote may keep the annotation, change it or drop it.

items.title: Deprecating a key or an element
items.text:
To retire a values key, keep it in the element's values.yaml, still working, and end the comment above it with one line in exactly this form:

stack/metallb/values.yaml
    config:
      # Address pools by name.
      # Deprecated: use config.ipAddressPools; removed in 2.0.0
      pools: {}

The comment is the key's description, so the element README shows it. The validator warns (POLICY039) on every values layer and fleet file that sets the key, naming the replacement and the version, and keeps accepting the key (POLICY035) until it is gone. A Deprecated: line in any other form is reported at the values.yaml. In a stable element, remove the key no earlier than that major, and at least one minor and 90 days after the release that deprecated it. A preview element may name the next minor instead, or rename the key without deprecating it (Deprecation). lifecycle/values.yaml keys are deprecated the same way, with a framework version, but at every maturity: removed in names a major, and the key keeps working until then (Lifecycle).

To retire an element, set deprecated: true in its Chart.yaml and keep it working until a later release removes it: any later minor for a preview element, a major for a stable one. The validator warns (POLICY092) on every values file that turns it on. Never rename an element directory: a rename deletes and recreates every Policy it renders. Add the new element and deprecate the old one.

items.title: Eject or contribute
items.text:
An element copied from upstream is tracked: its .copier-answers.yml names the release, and copier update merges each upstream release you take with your edits (Element updates).

  • Change it through values when you can. Every config key, policy, template and operator can be set or turned off from a layer, and layers never conflict with updates.
  • Contribute a change every adopter needs: a fix, a missing config key, a new converter. Once it is released, the element update brings it back to you, and the element stays supported (Contributing).
  • Eject when your copy has diverged for good: git rm stack/<element>/.copier-answers.yml. The element is then yours like one you wrote; no updates arrive, and upstream no longer supports it (Tiers).

An element you write with create-element.sh has no answers file, so copier never touches it.

items.title: Element reference
items.text:
stack/<element>/README.md is generated from Chart.yaml, values.yaml and converters/. Don't edit it.

pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python tools/doc-generator.py                   # every element without a .copier-answers.yml
python tools/doc-generator.py --element <name>  # one element
python tools/doc-generator.py --check           # report stale ones, write nothing

Without --element, the generator skips elements copied from upstream (those with a .copier-answers.yml). Their README comes with each release, so a framework update with a newer generator doesn't rewrite them and make them count as modified. If you edit a tracked element's Chart.yaml, values.yaml or converters, run --element <name> yourself; its README then merges with upstream's on each update like any other edited file. After you eject an element, the next run regenerates its README.

Source Shown as Chart.yaml description Lead paragraph Chart.yaml home Link at the top of the README. Set it to the element's page on the docs site if it has one; leave it out otherwise Chart.yaml annotation policystk.io/stability Stability: line under the lead paragraph, linking Element stability. Left out when the annotation is absent Comment above config: Settings intro Comment above a key under config That row's description description: of a policy, template or operator Policy line or template row enabled: false entries Optional pieces table

A blank line between a comment and its key keeps the comment out, for maintainer notes. When the hook and CI run the generator: Hooks.

items.title: Validation
items.text:
tools/validator is a Go program that renders every element (a Helm chart under stack/, How an element is built) the way Argo CD will, then checks the sources and the result against the validator rules. CI runs it on every PR (Policy Validate). This page is for element authors and for anyone fixing a finding.

The validator exists because most PolicyStack mistakes are silent or show up late, on a managed cluster:

  • Argo CD skips a values file that doesn't exist, so a typo in a fleet file's valueFiles (the list of values files a cluster reads) silently drops that layer (POLICY050, POLICY052).
  • A converter (a template file under an element's converters/) that reads a config key nobody set renders null, not an error (POLICY022).
  • The hub accepts any typo inside a Policy's policy-templates, such as remediationAction: enforec; it only fails on the managed cluster (POLICY080, CRD schemas).
  • ACM templates (the escaped {{ "{{" }} ... {{ "}}" }} parts of a converter) are resolved by ACM after Helm, so helm template never runs them (POLICY081).
  • ACM rejects a Policy whose hub copy, pstack.<policy>-<element>-<cluster>, is over 63 characters. The name grows with the cluster name, so it only fails for long cluster names (POLICY001, Naming limits).

items.title: What it checks
items.text:
The validator never talks to a cluster. It stands in for the fleet with fixtures: made-up fleet files in tools/validator/testdata/clusters (see Fixtures). For each element and each fixture it builds the same values cascade the ApplicationSet builds (Order) and runs helm template with it. It also renders lifecycle/, the chart a hub uses to build and destroy clusters, for fixtures that set hub: (the hub that builds them), as release lifecycle-<cluster> (Cluster lifecycle).

Every rule runs in one of three phases:

Phase Runs Reads Rules Chart Once per element The element's own Chart.yaml, values.yaml and converters/ POLICY021, 022, 030, 031, 040, 070, 090 Cluster Once per element and fixture The helm template output for that cascade POLICY001, 002, 032, 033, 034, 037, 050, 080, 081, 082, RENDER000 Repo Once Every element, every file under values/, every fleet file, install/, the copier answers files POLICY003, 011, 035, 038, 039, 051, 052, 060, 061, 071, 091, 092

Cluster-phase rules see the whole cascade, so a values layer that turns a template on or changes its action is checked the same as the element's own values.yaml.

items.title: Running it
items.text:
You need the tools from mise.toml on your PATH (Setup), plus make and git. The first run builds the validator, which downloads its Go modules (or reads them from GOPROXY); after that it runs offline: the CRDs are committed in tools/validator/crds/ (CRD schemas), and policy-library, the Helm library chart every element depends on, comes from lib/policy-library in the same checkout (Library changes).

While writing an element (Workflow):

make -C tools/validator preview ELEMENT=metallb CLUSTER=nonprod-west-1 # (1)!
make -C tools/validator validate ELEMENT=metallb # (2)!
  1. Renders one element for one fixture and prints it. ELEMENT is the chart name (stack/<name>). CLUSTER is the fixture's file name without directory or .yaml: CLUSTER=acm-dc1 for hubs/acm-dc1.yaml.
  2. Every rule, for one element. Repo-phase rules still load everything but report only this element's findings, so findings that belong to no element (POLICY052, POLICY071) don't show.

Before opening a PR, run validate, which is what ci runs in your repository. For a PR to upstream PolicyStack, run its validator CI instead (every CI job: Setup):

make -C tools/validator ci # (1)!
  1. lint, validate, then test. Upstream only: test reads upstream's test data, which copier leaves out of your repository.

items.title: Preview
items.text:
preview writes a temporary values file holding only stack.<key>.enabled: true (<key> is ELEMENT in camelCase: user-monitoring → userMonitoring) and appends it, with baseline.yaml, on top of the fixture's cascade. Only the element switch is forced: policies, templates and operators shipped enabled: false stay off unless the fixture's layers turn them on. To preview one, set its enabled: true in the fixture's values/clusters/<fixture>.yaml for the run. It runs only RENDER000 and POLICY081, so it prints output even when other rules would fail (run validate for those). It prints two files:

  • <element>.yaml: the Placement, PlacementBinding and Policies after Helm. The Placement selects name Exists (from the baseline), not the single cluster Argo CD would target (Placement).
  • <element>.evaluated.yaml: the objects each ConfigurationPolicy would apply, with ACM templates resolved on an empty cluster (ACM templates). Each object is headed by its ConfigurationPolicy name and complianceType. A template that fails is listed first as # POLICY081 <name>: <error>. An object whose template looks up something the empty cluster lacks is written as rendered, marked looks up an object the cluster lacks. OperatorPolicies are not expanded; only their -ns and -status ConfigurationPolicies appear.
nonprod-west-1/metallb.evaluated.yaml (excerpt)
---
# addressing-pools (mustonlyhave)
apiVersion: metallb.io/v1beta1
kind: IPAddressPool
metadata:
  name: services
  namespace: metallb-system
spec:
  addresses:
  - 10.20.30.100-10.20.30.120
  autoAssign: true
---
# install-metallb-ns (musthave)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: metallb-system

Without CLUSTER, preview renders every fixture and prints only the paths it wrote. The files go to a new temporary directory, which is not deleted, or to PREVIEW=<dir> (relative to tools/validator). ELEMENT=my-element previews the sample element.

copier leaves the fixtures out of your repository, so there preview renders your fleet files instead, and CLUSTER names one of them (CLUSTER=<hubName> for fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml).

items.title: What validate runs
items.text:
validate builds the binary, then runs the validator in three passes. All of them run, and any failure fails the target. Passes 1 and 2 render the fixtures, so they run only where tools/validator/testdata/clusters exists: upstream has it, an adopter's copy doesn't.

  1. Fixtures. Every element plus tools/sample-element/, which tools/create-element.sh copies for every new element and so must stay valid. Skips POLICY052, because fixture revisions are not real pins, and POLICY081, which pass 2 covers. It runs POLICY071, the install chart check.
  2. Profiles. The all-on run, then one run per file in tools/validator/testdata/profiles/. Together they turn every element and optional piece on, so POLICY081 and POLICY001 see every converter (Profiles).
  3. Your fleet. Only when fleet/*.yaml or fleet/hubs/*.yaml exists, which upstream never has. It renders the real fleet files and is the only pass that runs POLICY052 against real revision pins. Without fixtures, it also runs POLICY071, so an adopter's copy checks install/ once it has a fleet file.

Upstream, a clean run prints ok: no findings three times (fixtures, all-on, variants). An adopter's copy prints it once, for fleet/.

Target Runs validate [ELEMENT=<chart>] The three passes above preview ELEMENT=<chart> [CLUSTER=<name>] [PREVIEW=<dir>] Preview crds Refetches the committed CRD schemas in tools/validator/crds/ from the pinned SHAs. Run it by hand after a pin changes, then commit the result test Upstream only. go test -race ./.... Tests that need Helm skip without it. A rule ID missing from the rules table in tools/validator/README.md (which Validator rules includes) fails lint golangci-lint (.golangci.yml, gofmt and goimports included; make fmt fixes formatting), go mod tidy -diff, go tool govulncheck ci Upstream only. lint, validate, test deps helm dependency update for every chart that uses policy-library. Optional: validate runs it for any chart whose charts/ archive is older than lib/

CI is the environment variable GitHub Actions sets. Leave it unset locally. When it is set, findings print as GitHub annotations (--github), missing CRDs fail the run instead of skipping POLICY080, and tests that would skip fail instead. test and lint check the validator itself, so only upstream's CI runs them, and test fails in a copy, which lacks upstream's test data (Upstream).

Note

Every run starts with helm dependency update on each chart, once per run, with --skip-refresh when every dependency is file://. It packages lib/policy-library into the chart's charts/, so the render always uses the library in your checkout, even when its version has not changed. When lib/policy-library does not satisfy the chart's version floor, the update fails, RENDER000 reports the element unrendered, and POLICY060 says what to change.

items.title: Baseline
items.text:
In production the ApplicationSet adds selector, the label selector that makes the element's Placement pick its one cluster (Placement), to every element's values. Outside Argo CD nothing does, and policy-library reads it unconditionally, so an enabled element fails:

error RENDER000 [metallb/nonprod-west-1] hint: cascade did not provide `selector`. ...
... at <$root.Values.selector.matchExpressions>: nil pointer evaluating interface {}.matchExpressions

validate and preview pass --extra-values tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml, which supplies a selector matching every cluster. A disabled element renders nothing, so it never hits this.

tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml
selector:
  matchExpressions:
    - key: name
      operator: Exists

--extra-values files are appended after values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml, so they win over every cascade file. They are never applied to lifecycle/, which ships its own selector. Argo CD passes the whole fleet file to lifecycle/ as values, so the validator appends the fixture there instead. For elements, the validator passes the fixture's version and channel as the ApplicationSet does.

items.title: Reading the output
items.text:
Each finding is <severity> <rule> [<element>[/<cluster>]] <message>, then at <file>:<line>:<col>:

error POLICY022 [metallb] reads config key pools, which is not in stack.metallb.config of the element's values.yaml or the config of a template rendering it
    at /path/to/policystack/stack/metallb/converters/addressing/pools.yaml:7:19
error POLICY033 [metallb] policies.addressing.templates.l2: pruneObjectBehavior with a dependency (the Policy's dependencies): ACM deletes this template whenever the dependency is unmet, and prune deletes its objects
    at /path/to/policystack/values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml:28:34
warning POLICY021 [metallb] converters/metallb-cr.yaml is never rendered: it is not converters/<policy>/<template>.yaml of a template and no templates.<t>.file names it
    at /path/to/policystack/stack/metallb/converters/metallb-cr.yaml:1

2 error(s), 1 warning(s)

Each points at the file to change: POLICY022 at the converter that reads the missing key, POLICY033 at the layer that set pruneObjectBehavior, POLICY021 at the stray file. Fixes for these and other common findings: Fixing common findings.

Only findings about one fixture name it: POLICY001, POLICY002, POLICY050, POLICY051, POLICY082 and RENDER000. POLICY033, POLICY037, POLICY080 and POLICY081 leave it out on purpose, so one mistake is reported once rather than once per fixture.

A finding on rendered output points at the last cascade file that sets the field on the entry (a policies.<p>, policies.<p>.templates.<t> or operatorPolicies.<k> key), else the file that defines the entry, else the template's converter. That is how the POLICY033 above lands on the cluster's values file, not the element. If no entry renders the object, it points at the fleet file; POLICY080 points at the element's values.yaml instead.

Exit Meaning 0 No errors. Warnings alone pass 1 Errors, or warnings with --severity warning 2 The validator failed, e.g. Helm not on PATH or an unknown --only/--skip rule ID Flags, for running the binary by hand

make fixes the flags it passes, so these only matter when you run tools/validator/bin/policystack-validator --repo-root . yourself. --help lists the rest.

Flag Effect --element Check and render one chart, by chart name --cluster Render one fleet file, by cluster name --evaluate With --render-dir, also write <chart>.evaluated.yaml --only / --skip Comma-separated rule IDs to run / skip --severity warning Fail on warnings too --github GitHub Actions annotations --fixtures-dir Fleet files to render, hubs in its hubs/. Default tools/validator/testdata/clusters; pass 3 passes fleet --extra-values Comma-separated values files appended to every cascade but lifecycle/'s (Baseline) --all-on Turns on every element and every policy, template and operator in it, ranked below --extra-values (Profiles) --lifecycle-dir Lifecycle chart, default <repo>/lifecycle --base-branch The branch a PR merges into, default $GITHUB_BASE_REF. POLICY052 resolves a revision naming it to HEAD, the PR's merge commit --render-dir Writes <dir>/<fleet file path without .yaml>/<element>.yaml, a failed render as # RENDER000: lines. Render Diff diffs two of these

Locally $GITHUB_BASE_REF is empty, so a fleet file with revision: main resolves to origin/main as of your last git fetch, not your working tree, and a branch you haven't pushed fails POLICY052. Pass --base-branch main to make main mean HEAD. POLICY052 also needs full history: tags and origin/* branches.

tools/validator/bin/policystack-validator resolve-revision [--branch <b> --at <commit>] -- <revision> prints the commit POLICY052 resolves a revision to, exit 1 when it does not resolve.

items.title: Fixtures
items.text:
tools/validator/testdata/clusters holds example fleet files for fake clusters that exist only for CI. Nothing is deployed. They list real files under values/, so a change to a shared layer such as values/environments/prod.yaml changes what every fixture listing it renders.

Upstream only

copier leaves tools/validator/testdata/clusters and upstream's values/ out of your repository, so the fixture and profile passes don't run there, and nothing in your values/ is read by a fixture.

The file name is the cluster name: hubs/acm-dc1.yaml renders as acm-dc1 and reads values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml. A fixture that sets hub names the hub that builds it with lifecycle/ (Cluster lifecycle), so the validator also renders lifecycle/ for it.

Upstream contributors add a fixture for a new fleet shape, such as a new lifecycle engine. In your repository, pass 3 checks your fleet/ files; you don't add fixtures for them. TestLoadDir_testdata (internal/fixtures) and TestResolve_testdata (internal/cascade) pin the exact list, so add the new file to both.

Fixture list Fixture Covers prod-east-1, nonprod-west-1 Imported managed clusters, version and channel hubs/acm-dc1 The hub the lifecycle fixtures name hcp-kubevirt, hcp-agent HyperShift hive-aws Hive on AWS hive-vsphere Hive on vSphere, one failure domain, DHCP sno-edge SiteConfig single-node bm-ha SiteConfig three masters and a worker hcp-retired, hive-retired, sno-retired state: absent name-budget-30-characters-long The 30-character name every element must fit (Naming limits)

items.title: ACM templates
items.text:
A converter's escaped {{ "{{" }} ... {{ "}}" }} parts are ACM templates: Helm prints them as text, and ACM resolves hub templates on the hub and the rest on the managed cluster (Helm templates and ACM templates, ACM policies in brief). helm template never runs them.

POLICY081 runs both stages with go-template-utils, the library ACM uses, against a fake cluster:

  1. Hub templates, as the propagator does. Lookups stay in the Policy's namespace, plus the cluster's own ManagedCluster, unless the Policy sets hubTemplateOptions.serviceAccountName.
  2. Managed templates, as the config-policy-controller does: object-templates-raw as a whole, each object-templates entry separately with skipObject.

The fake cluster holds no objects and serves only the kinds listed in kinds in tools/validator/internal/acmtemplates/acmtemplates.go. The fake hub also holds the operator-owned objects listed in hubObjects there: today one, Route stackrox/central, because stack/acs/converters/secured/agents.yaml does index into it on the hub.

It fails on an undefined function (in any branch), a failed call such as index on nil, a hub lookup outside the Policy's namespace, a kind the fake cluster does not serve (a misspelled kind or apiVersion), and output with <no value> or an object missing apiVersion/kind:

error POLICY081 [acs] central-console (managed template): resolves to <no value>: a field the template reads is missing
    at /path/to/policystack/stack/acs/converters/central/console.yaml:10

Missing objects. On an empty cluster every lookup misses. How that ends depends on the function:

  • fromSecret, fromConfigMap and copySecretData of a missing object stop evaluation. That is not a failure, because on a real cluster another policy or operator creates the object. Code after it is parsed but not run, so only an undefined function there is caught; a bad index or missing field after a fromSecret shows up only on the cluster.
  • lookup of a missing object returns an empty map and evaluation continues, so what you do with the result decides. These fail the same way on a real cluster before the object exists:
Template Result $host := (lookup ... "central").spec.host then https://$host POLICY081: resolves to <no value> $host := index (lookup ... "central") "spec" "host" POLICY081: index of nil pointer $host := dig "spec" "host" "" (lookup ... "central") Passes, $host is "" .spec.host as above, then skipObject (not $host) before printing it Passes, the object is skipped until the Route exists

ACS uses the last form, because a ConsoleLink with an empty href is worse than none:

stack/acs/converters/central/console.yaml
href: '{{ "{{" }} $host := (lookup "route.openshift.io/v1" "Route" "stackrox" "central").spec.host {{ "}}" }}{{ "{{" }} skipObject (not $host) {{ "}}" }}https://{{ "{{" }} $host {{ "}}" }}'

Looking up a new kind, or indexing a new hub object

Add the kind to kinds in acmtemplates.go, or POLICY081 fails with one or more API resources are not installed. A hub template that indexes into an operator-owned hub object needs that object in hubObjects.

items.title: Profiles
items.text:
Fixtures leave most elements off, and every optional piece (a policy, template or operator shipped enabled: false, Optional pieces) stays off, so most converters never render under the fixtures. Pass 2 of validate turns everything on so POLICY081 and POLICY001 reach every converter:

  • All-on run. --all-on turns on every element under stack/ (and tools/sample-element with --include-sample-element) and every policy, template and operator in it, over any layer that turns one off. The validator builds this from the elements at run time, so a new element or enabled: false entry needs nothing added. tools/validator/testdata/inputs.yaml is layered on top: the inputs below, and the few choices all-on can't make, such as infra-nodes restore.
  • One run per file in tools/validator/testdata/profiles/, each layered alone over the baseline, without --all-on. variants.yaml holds settings that can't be on together with the all-on run. Example: infra-nodes workloads and restore exclude each other, so variants.yaml turns workloads off and restore on.

Every rule but POLICY052 and POLICY071 runs on these, so an optional piece also needs its input. A converter that loops over a config map renders nothing when the map is empty (Converter shapes): metallb's addressing/pools.yaml ranges over config.ipAddressPools. With the map empty it renders object-templates-raw: [], and a Policy whose templates are all empty is reported Compliant by ACM while checking nothing, which POLICY082 fails. inputs.yaml therefore sets metallb.config.ipAddressPools and the other maps:

tools/validator/testdata/inputs.yaml
stack:
  metallb:
    config:
      ipAddressPools: {internal: {addresses: [192.168.100.1-192.168.100.20]}}

A Policy with only some empty templates passes.

TestProfileCoverage, run by make test, fails for a converter under stack/ with ACM templates that neither the all-on run nor a profile renders. Profiles never reach lifecycle/ (extra values are not applied there), so a change to a lifecycle converter's ACM template needs a test case in tools/validator/internal/acmtemplates (hypershift_test.go, hive_test.go, siteconfig_test.go, ...), which resolves it against fake hub objects so the branches for an existing cluster run too.

items.title: CRD schemas
items.text:
The hub's API server validates a Policy, Placement and PlacementBinding at sync, but not the ConfigurationPolicy, OperatorPolicy or CertificatePolicy inside policy-templates: the Policy CRD declares objectDefinition with x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields. A bad field there passes the hub and only fails on the managed cluster. POLICY080 runs the CRD validation for those embedded objects at PR time.

It checks rendered objects against the CRDs ACM 2.16 serves, the oldest release PolicyStack supports. The checks run in-process (k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver) the way the API server's do: prune unknown fields, apply defaults, validate. InformOnly is read as inform, because the ConfigurationPolicy CRD's enum lacks it and ACM's framework add-on translates it. The CRDs are committed in tools/validator/crds/ (7 files, about 130 KB), fetched by make crds at the SHAs pinned in tools/validator/Makefile:

Repo Branch CRDs stolostron/governance-policy-propagator release-2.16 Policy, PlacementBinding, PolicySet stolostron/config-policy-controller release-2.16 ConfigurationPolicy, OperatorPolicy stolostron/cert-policy-controller release-2.16 CertificatePolicy open-cluster-management-io/api release-1.2 (v1.2.0, what the propagator requires) Placement

Committed, they need no network at validation time, which keeps disconnected sites working. --crds-dir overrides the directory. Without CRDs, POLICY080 is skipped with a warning, or fails the run when CI is set. The run logs how many objects were validated.

Bumping and adding

Upstream, Renovate moves each *_SHA to its branch head. Moving to a new ACM floor means changing the branch= comments and SHAs by hand. To add a CRD, add its raw URL to CRD_URLS, plus a # renovate: comment and *_SHA line for a new repo. After any of these, run make crds and commit tools/validator/crds/: upstream CI refetches the pinned files and fails while they differ, so a Renovate SHA bump stays red until someone does. Resolve the SHA with git ls-remote https://github.com/<repo> refs/heads/<branch>.

items.title: Destructive templates
items.text:
POLICY037 fails a template that is mustonlyhave or mustnothave (ConfigurationPolicy) on an object OpenShift owns (list in the POLICY037 row): enforced, it wipes what the installer and operators wrote. Use musthave.

A template that must stay mustonlyhave or mustnothave can only be InformOnly (reported, never enforced); an element has no way to enforce it. The validator also honours validator.policystk.io/allow-destructive: "<reason>" on a ConfigurationPolicy, but policy-library can't set it today.

items.title: Advanced Cluster Security
items.text:
The acs element installs Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (ACS) and registers clusters with it. ACS has two parts:

  • Central: the UI, API, database and scanners. It runs once, on the ACM hub.
  • Secured cluster: the agents on every cluster you want protected. Sensor watches the cluster and connects to Central; Collector and Admission Controller run alongside it.

A new secured cluster proves itself to Central once, with a cluster registration secret (CRS). You generate one CRS on the hub, following Red Hat's CRS procedure, and the element copies it to every cluster. Sensor uses it to register, gets its own certificates back and renews them itself, so the CRS expiring, being replaced or revoked never affects a cluster that has already registered.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• ACS 4.9 or later. CRS registration is GA from 4.10; on 4.9 it is Technology Preview but works with this element.
  • A default StorageClass on the hub. Central's database PVC stackrox-db uses it; without one Central never starts and central-central-ready stays NonCompliant.
  • Generating a CRS needs the ACS Admin role.
  • Every secured cluster must reach Central's Route on the hub on port 443.

items.title: Turn it on
items.text:
enabled: true installs the operator. policies.central and policies.secured are the element's two optional Policies (How an element is built); turn on the role each cluster plays. Both ship off.

HubSecured clusters

In a layer only the hub reads: values/clusters/<hubName>.yaml (the hub's hubName), or a file such as values/acm/<hubName>.yaml that only hub fleet files list (Hub file). Turning central on for any other cluster starts a second Central there that no cluster registers with.

stack:
  acs:
    enabled: true
    policies:
      central:
        enabled: true
      secured: # (1)!
        enabled: true
  1. Optional. It makes ACS monitor the hub itself. Other managed clusters don't need it.

In any layer those clusters read, for example values/environments/prod.yaml.

stack:
  acs:
    enabled: true
    policies:
      secured:
        enabled: true

Central must run on the ACM hub: the secured Policy reads the CRS and Central's Route from the hub (How the CRS reaches each cluster). Until central runs there and you have generated the CRS, secured-tls on every secured cluster is NonCompliant with a template-error.

Settings (auth, scanner sizing, SecurityPolicies, admission control) are in the element's README. The defaults:

  • OpenShift login, with the cluster-admins group mapped to the ACS Admin role and no role for other users (Access).
  • Three SecurityPolicies: no privilege escalation, no root user, no shell spawning.
  • Admission control enforcement off, because the webhook sits in every deployment's path. The operator's own default is on.

items.title: Access
items.text:
Users log in to Central with their OpenShift account. A user gets config.auth.minimumRole plus every role mapped to each OpenShift group they belong to (oc get groups), so groups synced from LDAP work too. config.auth.groups maps a group to a list of roles:

stack:
  acs:
    config:
      auth:
        groups:
          cluster-admins: # (1)!
            - Admin
          sec-ops:
            - Analyst
            - Vulnerability Management Approver
          ci-bots:
            - Continuous Integration
  1. The default. Groups from every layer merge, so a cluster's file can add a group without repeating this one. Set it to null to remove it.

Roles are names of existing ACS roles, case-sensitive: the system roles listed under Platform Configuration > Access Control > Roles. The mapping lands in ConfigMap stackrox/acs-declarative-configs, which Central reloads on change without a restart.

Read-only in the UI

Central owns everything in the declarative config. The OpenShift auth provider and its group rules can't be edited in the ACS UI; change them in values.

Failures

  • A role name that doesn't exist doesn't fail the Policy. Central skips the rule and reports it under Platform Configuration > System Health > Declarative configuration.
  • A group given as a string (sec-ops: Analyst) instead of a list fails the render with range can't iterate over Analyst.
  • auth.provider: "" drops the declarative config, and with it every group mapping. Only the admin user from Secret stackrox/central-htpasswd can log in.

items.title: What it creates
items.text:
<cluster> is the ManagedCluster name, or hubName on the hub (Rendered names). Every Policy enforces. Templates marked (InformOnly) only report, even inside an enforcing Policy (inform, enforce and InformOnly).

Policy Where Templates install-acs-<cluster> Every cluster with enabled: true install-acs-ns, install-acs (OperatorPolicy, package rhacs-operator, channel stable), install-acs-status (reports only, The install Policy) central-acs-<hubName> The hub central-central (namespace stackrox, Central stackrox-central-services, auth config), central-central-ready (InformOnly), central-policies (SecurityPolicies, after central-central-ready), central-crs-ready (InformOnly), central-hub-access, central-console (console link) secured-acs-<cluster> Every secured cluster secured-tls (the CRS copy), secured-agents (SecuredCluster stackrox-secured-cluster-services, after secured-tls), secured-agents-ready (InformOnly)

central and secured stay Pending until install-acs-<cluster> is Compliant, so the operator is running before any ACS resource is written.

items.title: How the CRS reaches each cluster
items.text:
secured-tls holds a Secret whose data is the hub template {{hub copySecretData "stackrox" "cluster-registration-secret" hub}}. ACM resolves hub templates on the hub while it copies the Policy to each cluster (ACM policies in brief), so the CRS never sits in Git:

  1. The ACM policy propagator reads stackrox/cluster-registration-secret on the hub, as ServiceAccount acs-hub-templates. central-hub-access creates that ServiceAccount, a Role in stackrox that can read only this Secret and the central Route, and a ClusterRole to read ManagedClusters (the hub skip below reads their labels).
  2. It writes the data, encrypted, into the cluster's copy of secured-acs-<cluster>. The cluster decrypts it and creates stackrox/cluster-registration-secret. The hub skips this: its own SecuredCluster reads the original.
  3. secured-agents fills the SecuredCluster's centralEndpoint the same way, from the hub's Route stackrox/central plus :443, and its clusterName from the ManagedCluster name. You set neither. A missing Route is an error, never an empty endpoint.

The propagator watches what it read. Replacing the hub's Secret re-copies it to every cluster without a commit.

items.title: First run
items.text:
1. Merge the values above to the revision the hub's fleet file pins (move a tag or SHA pin, Promoting and rolling back). The operator installs, then Central deploys on the hub.
  2. Wait for central-central-ready to be Compliant: in the console, Governance > Policies > central-acs-<hubName>.
  3. Generate the CRS.
  4. Each secured cluster gets the copy, then its SecuredCluster, and turns Compliant.

Until step 3 these are not Compliant, and that is expected:

Template State Why central-crs-ready NonCompliant No CRS on the hub yet secured-tls, on every secured cluster NonCompliant The hub template can't find the Secret secured-agents Pending Waits for secured-tls, so no SecuredCluster exists yet secured-agents-ready NonCompliant No SecuredCluster, no Sensor

They clear on their own once the Secret exists.

items.title: Generate the CRS
items.text:
Run this from a shell logged in to the hub with oc. roxctl is the ACS CLI; install it first from Red Hat's ACS docs.

export ROX_ENDPOINT=$(oc -n stackrox get route central -o jsonpath='{.spec.host}'):443 # (1)!
export ROX_API_TOKEN=<token with the Admin role> # (2)!
roxctl central crs generate "fleet-$(date +%Y%m%d)" --valid-for 8760h --output crs.yaml # (3)!
oc apply -n stackrox -f crs.yaml
rm crs.yaml
  1. Every roxctl command on this page reads it. The Route serves Central's own certificate, so on x509: certificate signed by unknown authority also export ROX_CA_CERT_FILE=<file> holding key ca.pem of Secret stackrox/central-tls.
  2. Platform Configuration > Integrations > API Token. Or skip it and pass --password with the admin password from Secret stackrox/central-htpasswd.
  3. The CRS's name in Central. Central refuses a name already used by a CRS that isn't revoked, so the date keeps renewals unique. 8760h is one year.

crs.yaml is a Secret named cluster-registration-secret, the name the operator reads, with annotations that include crs.platform.stackrox.io/name, id and expires-at.

Set --valid-for

Without it the CRS lasts 24 hours and central-crs-ready is NonCompliant from the start (Health).

Any other way of writing the Secret works, an ExternalSecret from your secret store for example, as long as it also writes the crs.platform.stackrox.io/expires-at annotation (with the External Secrets Operator: spec.target.template.metadata.annotations). Without it, central-crs-ready stays NonCompliant forever.

items.title: Health
items.text:
Template Policy Compliant means central-crs-ready central-acs-<hubName> The hub holds the CRS with over 90 days left, so a CRS valid for 90 days or less never is. Checked daily, every 10 minutes while NonCompliant. A one-year CRS turns NonCompliant about 9 months after you generate it secured-tls secured-acs-<cluster> The cluster holds the copy. Turns NonCompliant on every cluster at once when the hub's Secret is gone secured-agents-ready secured-acs-<cluster> The SecuredCluster is deployed and Sensor is ready. A refused or expired registration shows up here, because Sensor never becomes ready

Not detected

A cluster still holding certificates from another Central (moved to another hub, Central reinstalled with a new CA) reports ready while it is disconnected. Check Platform Configuration > Clusters in ACS.

items.title: Renew or rotate
items.text:
When central-crs-ready turns NonCompliant:

  1. Note the current CRS's name: oc -n stackrox get secret cluster-registration-secret -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.crs\.platform\.stackrox\.io/name}'. Applying the new one overwrites it.
  2. Run Generate the CRS again. The copies on every cluster follow.
  3. Optional: revoke the old one with roxctl central crs revoke <name>, with the exports from Generate the CRS. Do this right away after a leak. roxctl central crs list shows every CRS with its expiry.

Never delete the Secret

Replace it with oc apply instead. Registration doesn't need it again, but the operator reads cluster-registration-secret on every reconcile, expired or not. Without it, or the old init bundle secrets, the operator fails to reconcile the SecuredCluster (InitBundleSecretsMissingError), so setting changes stop reaching the agents. A deleted copy comes back at the next secured-tls evaluation; a deleted hub Secret turns secured-tls NonCompliant on every cluster and breaks the hub's own SecuredCluster.

After a Central reinstall the CRS is no longer valid. Generate a new one.

items.title: Re-register a cluster
items.text:
Central refuses a CRS for a cluster name that has connected before. In ACS, each cluster is named after its ManagedCluster; the hub is local-cluster unless ACM's localClusterName changed it.

A refused cluster shows secured-agents-ready NonCompliant, and the Sensor pod's CRS init container crash-loops (oc -n stackrox get pods -l app=sensor).

Event Steps Rebuilt or re-created under the same name, including lifecycle state: absent then re-added; SecuredCluster or stackrox namespace deleted 1 Moved to another hub; Central reinstalled 2, 3 Central restored from backup None if Sensor reconnects, else 1, 2, 3 Still refused The steps you skipped, in order 1, 2, 3
  1. Hub: delete the cluster's old record so Central accepts the name again. Platform Configuration > Clusters, or roxctl cluster delete --name <cluster> with the exports from Generate the CRS.
  2. Cluster: delete the certificates Sensor already holds, so it falls back to the CRS. oc -n stackrox get secret -o name | grep -E '/tls-cert-|/(sensor|collector|admission-control)-tls$' | xargs oc -n stackrox delete
  3. Cluster: restart Sensor so it registers. oc -n stackrox delete pod -l app=sensor

Step 2 is safe only once cluster-registration-secret is on the cluster; without it Sensor has nothing to register with.

items.title: Turning it off
items.text: Turning off secured, central or the element deletes their Policies but nothing they created: no template sets pruneObjectBehavior, the ACM setting that deletes a template's objects with its Policy (Removal and pruning). The operator, Central or SecuredCluster, the stackrox namespace and the CRS copy stay, and the cluster stays registered in Central. Re-enabling it picks up the existing SecuredCluster and Sensor keeps its registration. If the SecuredCluster or stackrox namespace was deleted in the meantime, or the cluster was rebuilt, follow Re-register a cluster.

items.title: Clusters registered with init bundles
items.text:
An init bundle is ACS's older registration method: TLS Secrets (sensor-tls, collector-tls, admission-control-tls) applied to each cluster. This section is for clusters that already run ACS agents registered with one, for example from before PolicyStack. New installs skip it. The element manages Central stackrox-central-services and SecuredCluster stackrox-secured-cluster-services in stackrox; yours must have those names, or the element creates second ones.

  1. Check the names: oc get central,securedcluster -A. Both must be in stackrox with the names above.
  2. Make sure the hub and every cluster run ACS 4.9 or later. Lift any operatorPolicies.acs.versions pin below that (Operator versions).
  3. Turn the element on, previewing step 4 with a dry run first, then merge and generate the CRS. Until you generate it, central-crs-ready and secured-tls are NonCompliant and the SecuredCluster isn't touched.
  4.
