The job runs twice. The leg that counts uses the Helm in mise.toml, 3.18.4: Argo CD renders every element with the Helm bundled in OpenShift GitOps, and OpenShift GitOps 1.18, the oldest PolicyStack supports, bundles Helm 3.18.4, so a pass here means the hub renders it too. The second leg uses Helm 4.2.1 to preview the next GitOps Helm. It is advisory (continue-on-error): its failure shows on the PR but doesn't fail ci. It becomes required when Argo CD 3.5 ships in OpenShift GitOps or Helm 3 reaches end of life on 2027-02-10, whichever comes first.

make -C tools/validator validate   # (1)!
  1. Three validator passes (What validate runs). POLICY080 reads the committed CRDs, so the job needs no network beyond Go modules.

Note

The Helm floor in mise.toml moves only when the supported OpenShift GitOps floor does (Installation). Upstream's Renovate does not bump it.

items.title: Your fleet (POLICY052)
items.text: The fleet/ pass renders your fleet files from the PR's tree, not each file's revision: a cluster pinned to tag v1.0 is validated against the PR's code. POLICY052 checks the pin itself: that it resolves and that its commit has what the fleet file uses (Revision). In a copier copy it also reads the framework release in .copier-answers.yml at that commit: a revision a major newer than the PR's, or more than one major older, fails, since the hub's install chart renders only its own major and the one before. To see what a pinned cluster actually gets, read Render Diff.

items.title: Install chart (POLICY071)
items.text:
install/ is run by hand on each hub, so nothing else renders it. Upstream checks it in the fixtures pass; your repository checks it in the fleet/ pass, so only once fleet/ has a file. It reads stack/acm and stack/gitops, which every repository needs. The check fails when:

  • helm lint install fails.
  • helm template install succeeds with an empty hubName or gitRepo. Neither has a usable default: hubName picks the hub's own fleet file and the clusters it builds, gitRepo is the repository Argo CD reads.
  • policyNamespace differs between install/values.yaml and values.yaml, which the elements read.
  • An ApplicationSet (or its Application template), the GitOpsCluster or its Placement lacks velero.io/exclude-from-backup: "true". ACM backup restores onto a passive hub, where a restored ApplicationSet would rebuild the old hub's clusters (Hub disaster recovery).
  • install/operators doesn't render the ACM and GitOps operators plus a MultiClusterHub (Installation).

items.title: Render Diff
items.text:
Comments on the PR with what the merge changes in each fleet/ cluster's rendered Policies. Upstream ships no fleet files, so this only does something in your repository. It never blocks a merge.

### Fleet render: 3 cluster(s) change

> [!WARNING]
> `edge-3` pins `v1.4`, which is not a tag, branch or commit. Merging stops Argo CD from generating Applications for every cluster until it is fixed.

| Cluster | Revision | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `prod-east-1` | `main` | user-monitoring: 1 Policy changed<br>metallb: 1 Policy added, 1 Policy removed<br>metallb: removes Policy `config-metallb-prod-east-1` |
| `nonprod-west-1` | `v1.0.0` → `main` | metallb: **render failed** |
| `edge-2` | new at `main` | 6 elements, 21 objects added |

items.title: What it renders
items.text:
Each fleet file is rendered at its own revision, resolved as POLICY052 does, once before and once after the merge (.github/scripts/render-diff.sh). A cluster is rendered only when its resolved commit or its fleet file changes. So a cluster pinned to main or HEAD shows the PR's changes, and a cluster pinned to a tag shows changes only when the PR edits its fleet file (revision, valueFiles, version, channel, install, hub). lifecycle/ is rendered for fleet files that set hub. install/ is not rendered: a change there reaches every cluster at the next helm upgrade (Install chart).

It renders with the baseline selector, so Placements show name Exists, not the per-cluster selector. It checks only that the render succeeds: findings come from Policy Validate.

items.title: Reading the comment
items.text:
Below the table, each cluster gets one collapsed block holding a diff per changed element, or the Helm error. render fixed means the element failed at the cluster's revision before the merge and renders now. removes Policy names each Policy the merge deletes from the hub, renames included: ACM names can't change, so a renamed Policy is deleted and recreated and starts its compliance history over. An element that fails the same way on both sides is not listed. A cluster added or removed shows totals only. A warning above the table flags a fleet file whose revision doesn't resolve or that the validator can't load at all. If it merges anyway, the ApplicationSet can't build its list of Applications: it deletes nothing, but no change reaches any cluster until the fleet file is fixed (Generators).

No fleet files, or no cluster whose render changes, means no comment. The comment is sticky: a later push that changes nothing deletes it.

Limits

  • Comments stop near 60,000 characters. The full patch is the run's render-diff.patch artifact.
  • A PR from another repository (a personal fork of yours) gets a read-only token, so the result goes to the job summary instead of a comment.
  • About 30 seconds per distinct commit rendered.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
Upstream, Renovate, a bot that opens dependency update PRs, bumps everything in the table below. Its config is the org preset renovate-config.json in PolicyStack/.github, which upstream's renovate.json extends. copier doesn't copy that file, and your repository runs no bot: the pins below reach you with framework updates (Upgrading PolicyStack).

Pinned in What mise.toml Every CLI tool, Go and Python tools/validator/go.mod Go libraries and govulncheck (go tool) tools/requirements*.txt PyYAML, Zensical .github/workflows/ Actions, by commit SHA tools/validator/Makefile The CRD source SHAs. A bump needs make crds and the refetched tools/validator/crds/ committed on the PR (CRD schemas)

policy-library is not a dependency Renovate moves: it is lib/policy-library in this repo, and elements declare a floor on it (Library changes).

items.title: Compatibility
items.text:
What upstream PolicyStack promises not to break, how each part is versioned, and what is checked automatically. Read it before you take an update you can't review line by line, or before you change a file copier manages. How updates arrive: Upgrading PolicyStack.

MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY are used as in RFC 2119.

items.title: Tiers
items.text:
Every path in your repository belongs to one tier. The tier decides who changes it, which version number it carries and what upstream promises about it.

Tier Paths Version Promise Framework install/, lifecycle/, lib/, tools/, the copied workflows and hooks, the root values.yaml, plus the surfaces in Public API vX.Y.Z, recorded in /.copier-answers.yml A breaking change is a framework major, except where Maturity lets a preview lifecycle engine change in a minor. You MUST NOT modify these paths: every framework update has to merge your edits, and a modified framework is not supported. Stable element Each stack/<element> whose Chart.yaml sets policystk.io/stability: stable (acm, gitops, upgrade), unmodified vX.Y.Z, the release it was copied from, recorded in stack/<element>/.copier-answers.yml A breaking change is a framework major (Element stability). Preview element Every other upstream element, policystk.io/stability: preview Same A framework minor MAY change values keys, Policy names or output, except the Policy names in Public API item 10. The release notes say how. Yours fleet/, values/, .github/CODEOWNERS, README.md, and every element you modified, ejected or wrote Yours None. Upstream never writes these after the first copy.

An element counts as unmodified while its files equal the tag in its answers file. Once you edit one, it is yours: updates still arrive, and your edits are merged with them (Resolving conflicts), but upstream supports it only if the problem reproduces on the unmodified element. To compare:

copier copy --vcs-ref "$(sed -n 's/^_commit: //p' stack/odf/.copier-answers.yml)" -d element=odf \
  https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git /tmp/odf
diff -r -x .copier-answers.yml -x charts -x Chart.lock /tmp/odf stack/odf # (1)!
  1. charts/ and Chart.lock are what helm dependency update writes, gitignored.

The tiers and paths in your repository: The repository.

items.title: Public API
items.text:
Within a framework major these change only by addition, except where an item says otherwise. A key, value, name or behaviour listed here is never removed, renamed or given a new meaning before the next major.

  1. Install chart. The values gitRepo, hubName and policyNamespace, the release name policystack in openshift-gitops, and the names of the objects it creates (Install chart).
  2. Values the ApplicationSets inject. version, channel, selector and policystack.libraryMajors into every Application; hub, state and install into lifecycle Applications (Order).
  3. Values cascade. The element's values.yaml, the root values.yaml, each valueFiles entry, then values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml, in that order. A missing file is skipped.
  4. Fleet files. fleet/<cluster>.yaml and fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml, with the keys revision, valueFiles, hub, state, install, version and channel (Fleet files). The top-level key apiVersion is reserved; a file without it is v1.
  5. Values schema. The top-level keys stack, global, placement, install and policyNamespace, and every key policy-library's schema accepts under stack.<element> (policy-library reference).
  6. Element authoring. include "policy-library.render" . and its .component override, policy-library.enabled, policy-library.clusterSuffix, the alias: stack dependency, discovery of converters/<policy>/<template>.yaml, _ partials, templates.<t>.file, .Config and the defaults chain (How an element is built). Every other policy-library.* define is internal.
  7. Rendered names. Applications <element>-<cluster> and lifecycle-<cluster>, Policies <policy>-<release>, ConfigurationPolicies <policy>-<template>, the install-<operator> templates, Placements, PlacementBindings and PolicySets, the pstack namespace, and the length budgets in Naming limits (Rendered names).
  8. Labels and annotations. The annotations lifecycle.policystk.io/hub and validator.policystk.io/allow-destructive, the Chart.yaml annotation policystk.io/stability and its values stable and preview, the label velero.io/exclude-from-backup, and the cluster labels in Labels.
  9. Tooling. Validator rule IDs, the make targets validate, preview and deps, tools/create-element.sh, the required checks ci and pr-title, the copier question element, and the tag format vX.Y.Z. A rule may be narrowed or retired in a minor; a change that makes it fail a repository that passes today follows Deprecation. A retired ID is never reused.
  10. Stable elements. Their config keys and types, the names of their policies, templates and operatorPolicies entries, Policy names other elements depend on, which entries are on by default, and the enforcement defaults enabled, remediationAction, complianceType and pruneObjectBehavior. Also the names of other elements' Policies that a stable element depends on, whatever their stability: today odf ready, which acm observability waits for.

items.title: Not covered
items.text:
These MAY change in any release:

  • Output of preview elements, even for unchanged values.
  • Internal library defines, and the internals of tools/*.py and tools/*.sh.
  • Validator message text. Rule IDs are covered; wording is not.
  • New validator warnings. A warning never fails a PR.
  • This documentation, and the example files under upstream's values/, which copier doesn't copy.
  • A change a security fix can't make compatibly. It is a fix without !, with a subject that starts with breaking:, and the release notes say what changed and why.

items.title: Versions
items.text:
The contract applies from v1.0.0. Prereleases (vX.Y.Z-rc.N) carry no promise: anything may change before the release they precede.

Upstream has one tag line, vX.Y.Z. Every release tag holds the framework and every element, and release-please cuts it from the Conventional Commit types merged since the last one (Releases). The release notes list every feat, fix, perf and revert, each element change under the element's name (odf:), and every ! change under its own heading. A breaking change to a preview element, or one Maturity allows in a minor for a preview engine, has no !: its subject starts with breaking: and says what to change, under the element's name or lifecycle, so searching for breaking: finds every one.

Part Version in Recorded in your repository Framework The tag, and install/Chart.yaml and lifecycle/Chart.yaml version /.copier-answers.yml _commit Element The tag only. stack/<element>/Chart.yaml version stays 0.1.0: nothing reads it, and it changes no output stack/<element>/.copier-answers.yml _commit policy-library lib/policy-library/Chart.yaml version, 4.x. Ships inside a framework release Nothing: it is part of the framework

Each copy keeps its own answers file, so you can update the framework and each element at different times. One rule orders them: an element's _commit MUST NOT be newer than the root _commit. Update the framework first, then the elements. An element on an older release than the framework keeps working within the same major; fixes to it still need an element update. After a framework major, update every element to it. POLICY061 fails an element newer than the framework or on another major.

items.title: Framework versions
items.text:
• Major: anything in Public API removed, renamed or given a new meaning; a breaking change to a stable element or a stable engine or platform; anything Lifecycle holds for a major at every maturity; a policy-library major; a naming or policyNamespace change.
  • Minor: a new optional key, injected value, fleet key, lifecycle engine or platform, validator rule, or a library minor; a new element; a compatible change to a stable element; any change to a preview element, breaking ones included; an incompatible change Maturity allows for a preview engine.
  • Patch: a fix.

A floor rise in Support is a minor.

items.title: Element stability
items.text:
policystk.io/stability in an element's Chart.yaml says what upstream promises about it. The element's generated README.md shows it near the top. An element you write may leave it out.

stack/acm/Chart.yaml
annotations:
  policystk.io/stability: stable
Stability Elements A breaking change ships in stable acm, gitops, upgrade A framework major only preview Every other upstream element, and every element tools/create-element.sh creates Any framework minor, except the Policy names in Public API item 10. The release notes say what to change

For a stable element, breaking means any of:

  • A config key removed, renamed, or narrowed to fewer types or values.
  • A policy, template or operator entry renamed.
  • An enforcement default flipped.
  • The library floor raised to a new library major.

A new key, a new policy or template that ships off or inform-only, a moved operator channel or version default, or a library floor raised within the major is a framework minor. A fix that leaves output for unchanged values identical, except for the bug, is a patch.

A preview element becomes stable in a framework minor, by changing its annotation. A stable element never goes back to preview within a major.

items.title: policy-library versions
items.text:
• Patch: a fix. Output for unchanged values changes only where it was a bug: it contradicts the library reference, or ACM rejects or misapplies it. The PR names the bug.
  • Minor: a new optional key or define. Output for values that don't set it is unchanged.
  • Major: anything removed or renamed, or any other change to output for unchanged values. A library major ships only in a framework major, and never changes the naming scheme.
  • Each element declares the lowest library it needs as a floor, version: "^4.N.0", and Helm refuses to render it against an older one (Library changes).

Each framework release holds one library major, in lib/policy-library. Elements you wrote move to a new library major when you take the framework major that ships it.

items.title: Hub and revision skew
items.text:
A hub runs one install chart, upgraded by hand, and renders every cluster at the revision its fleet file pins. Those revisions can be on older framework releases than the hub.

  • Same major: a hub on X.Y renders every revision from X.0 to X.Y. Upgrade the hub before moving any pin to a newer release: an element from that release may read a value only the newer install chart injects.
  • Across majors: a hub on N renders revisions on N and on the latest N-1 release. Move every pin to the latest N-1 release, upgrade the hubs to N, then move pins to N.

The order and commands: Framework updates.

items.title: Deprecation
items.text:
The Values keys and Elements rules below bind the Public API, stable elements and stable engines. A preview element SHOULD deprecate a key for one minor when the old key can keep working, and MAY rename or remove keys in any minor. install keys follow Lifecycle at every maturity.

  • Values keys: a deprecated key keeps working, and the schema and POLICY035 keep accepting it, for at least one minor and at least 90 days. It is removed only in a major. The key's comment ends with Deprecated: use <key>; removed in <version>, and POLICY039 warns on every layer and fleet file that still sets it (Deprecating a key).
  • Elements: a deprecated element sets deprecated: true in its Chart.yaml and keeps working until a release removes it: any later minor for a preview element, a major for a stable one. POLICY092 warns on every values file that turns it on. Once it is removed, copier update on it fails: eject it to keep it as yours, or remove it.
  • Validator rules: a new rule, or a new error case of an existing rule, that can fail a repository that passes today ships as a warning for at least one minor before it becomes an error. A rule that prevents an outage or a security problem MAY be an error at once. Rule IDs are never reused.
  • Fleet keys and injected values: only added within a major, at every maturity, install keys of preview engines included. A new fleet key is optional, and leaving it out keeps the old behaviour.

Fixes, security fixes included, land only in the latest minor. Older minors and majors get no backports: to get a fix, update. For a preview element, that update brings every change to it since your release, breaking ones included.

items.title: Policy names
items.text:
ACM can't rename a Policy. A changed name deletes the old Policy and creates a new one, which restarts its compliance history. What the cluster already has stays, unless the template sets pruneObjectBehavior (Removal and pruning).

  • Changing the naming scheme or policyNamespace is a framework major.
  • Renaming a policy, template or operator entry of a stable element is a framework major. The release notes list every Policy it recreates.
  • Element directories are never renamed. A replacement is a new element; the old one is deprecated and removed as in Deprecation.
  • For every cluster that still has a fleet file, Render Diff lists each Policy a PR removes, renames included. A removed fleet file shows totals only (Render Diff).

items.title: Lifecycle
items.text:
lifecycle/ is framework code and follows framework versions. "Engine" is install.engine; "platform" is install.platform for hypershift, the cloud under install.hive.platform for hive, and install.siteconfig.templates for siteconfig (Lifecycle keys).

At every maturity, these change only in a framework major:

  • The name or namespace of an object the hub creates: HostedCluster, NodePool <cluster>-<pool>, ClusterDeployment, ClusterInstance and their namespaces.
  • The default of any key Lifecycle keys marks fixed at create, and of engine, services and namespace.
  • An install key removed, renamed or given a new meaning. A preview engine that replaces a key deprecates the old one (Deprecation) and accepts both until the next major.

Fleet files are read at HEAD, and each revision's lifecycle/ rejects install keys it doesn't know. Set a new install key only on a fleet file whose revision has the release that added it.

For a stable engine or platform:

  • Patch: a fix.
  • Minor: a new optional key, engine or platform, or a validation every existing fleet file already passes.
  • Major: any other incompatible change, such as a converter that builds a different object from the same keys.

A renamed hub object can cost you a cluster

The lifecycle Policy finds what it built by name. Under a new name it creates a new object next to the old one: a second HostedCluster, ClusterDeployment or ClusterInstance, or a second NodePool, while the old one keeps running unmanaged. Getting back means destroying one of them by hand. A Policy rename costs compliance history; this can cost a cluster. Read the lifecycle section of a framework major's notes before any hub that builds clusters renders it.

Not covered at any maturity: hostedCluster, nodePools, hive.installConfig and hive.clusterDeployment. They are merged into Red Hat's objects as you write them, and follow the HyperShift and Hive APIs.

items.title: Maturity
items.text:
Stable engines and platforms follow the rules above. Apart from the rules that hold at every maturity, a preview one MAY change incompatibly in a framework minor: its converters, behaviour and defaults not fixed at create. The release notes say what to change. Promotion to stable happens in a minor once its build, upgrade, scale and destroy paths have been checked on live clusters.

Engine Platform Maturity hypershift KubeVirt Preview hypershift Agent Preview hypershift None Preview hive aws Preview hive gcp Preview hive azure Preview hive vsphere Preview siteconfig ai Preview siteconfig ibi Preview

Every engine and platform is preview at 1.0

Pin hub-built clusters to tags, and read the lifecycle section of every framework release's notes before moving their pins (Rolling out changes).

items.title: How it is enforced
items.text: Rule Check An element gets the library it needs Helm's ^4.N.0 constraint on the file:// dependency. Helm's error is generic (can't get a valid version for 1 subchart(s)); POLICY060 names the fix The library version moves with every library change ct lint --check-version-increment in upstream CI. It checks that version rose, not by how much: the lib/tests snapshot diff and review decide patch, minor or major Fleet pins stay inside the skew window POLICY052 reads /.copier-answers.yml at each revision: newer than the branch's major, or more than one major older, fails. Yours to check: that an N-1 pin is the latest N-1 release, and that hubs are upgraded before pins move A hub never renders a library major it wasn't built for The install chart injects policystack.libraryMajors; policy-library fails the render when its own major isn't listed Answers files say what was copied POLICY061: every _commit is a vX.Y.Z tag, each element's names its own directory, and no element's is newer than the root's or on another major Stability is stable or preview tools/doc-generator.py, run by the element-readmes hook, fails on any other value. It skips elements with a .copier-answers.yml, so in your repository it checks only elements you wrote or ejected A breaking change gets a major Review only. The PR author marks it with !, a reviewer checks it, and release-please bumps the major. Upstream has no fleet files, so Render Diff shows the change only in your repository: on the update PR for clusters pinned to the default branch, and on the PR that moves a tag pin Deprecation windows Review only. POLICY039 warns on a deprecated key, but doesn't check the version its comment names A new error ships as a warning first Review only A preview break says breaking: Review only. pr-title accepts any subject Tags never move GitHub tag rulesets on v* in upstream Conflict markers never merge The check-merge-conflict hook in ci, over every file except tools/validator/crds/, and the render in validate

items.title: Support
items.text:
PolicyStack is community-supported. Red Hat supports OpenShift, ACM and OpenShift GitOps, not PolicyStack.

PolicyStack OpenShift ACM OpenShift GitOps Helm 1.x 4.20 or later 2.16 or later 1.18 or later (Argo CD 3.1) 3.18.4, as bundled in GitOps 1.18. Helm 4 is tested, advisory

CI runs no cluster. It renders with Helm 3.18.4, plus Helm 4.2.1 as an advisory leg, and validates the output against the ACM 2.16 CRDs. OpenShift and OpenShift GitOps are not tested. Later versions are expected to work, and a problem on one is fixed like any other bug.

Supported means a bug that reproduces on the latest release, with the framework and the element unmodified, on versions in the table above, is accepted as a bug. Fixes are best effort, with no response time, and land only in the latest minor (Deprecation).

A floor rises in a framework minor, and only after Red Hat's Maintenance Support for that version ends. For an OpenShift EUS release, that is the end of Maintenance Support, not of the EUS terms. The minor before announces it: a maintainer adds the line to that release's GitHub notes and to the table here. The Helm floor is the Helm the GitOps floor bundles, and rises with it. Until a floor rises, a key, policy or template that needs a newer version ships off, and its comment or description names the version. Operator channel and version defaults follow Element stability.

Report vulnerabilities through private vulnerability reporting.

items.title: Fleet files
items.text:
A fleet file, fleet/<cluster>.yaml, enrolls one cluster: while it exists on the default branch, the hub creates that cluster's Applications, and its keys pick the Git revision they render and the values layers they read. What that means for delivery (why the file is read at HEAD while everything else is read at revision, how long a merge takes, what one broken file stops) is in How PolicyStack works.

Upstream ships no live fleet files; your repository adds them. Working examples are the validator fixtures in tools/validator/testdata/clusters/.

Imported clusterHub-built clusterHub 
# fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main # (1)!
channel: stable-4.20 # (2)!
valueFiles: # (3)!
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml
  1. Branch, tag or SHA. Every Application for this cluster renders stack/, values.yaml and values/ from this commit (Revision).
  2. Changes the cluster: the upgrade element, the one element enabled by default, enforces this as the cluster's ClusterVersion spec.channel as soon as the file merges (OpenShift upgrades). Leave it out to keep the cluster's current channel.
  3. Paths under values/, lowest precedence first (Order). values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml is always added last, so it is not listed. Any file under values/ works: a custom layer such as tenants/payments.yaml is just a file you list.
# fleet/hcp-kubevirt.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1 # (1)!
version: 4.20.8 # (2)!
valueFiles:
  - environments/nonprod.yaml
  - platforms/kubevirt.yaml # (3)!
  1. Names the hub that builds this cluster by its hubName, the name the hub got at install (helm install ... --set hubName=acm-dc1) (Cluster lifecycle). CI requires fleet/hubs/acm-dc1.yaml to exist, so a typo here can't leave the cluster with no hub to build or destroy it.
  2. Required with hub: it is the release the hub installs.
  3. Sets install (platform KubeVirt, two workers) for every cluster that lists it. A fleet file's own install is merged over it (Install keys).
# fleet/hubs/acm-dc1.yaml
revision: main
valueFiles: # (1)!
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/baremetal.yaml
  - acm/acm-dc1.yaml # (2)!
  1. The hub is a cluster like any other: every element these layers enable, at the action they set, runs on the hub too.
  2. Settings for the hub's own acm and gitops elements (Hand the operators to PolicyStack). Listed last, so only values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml overrides it. Hubs in one datacenter, such as an active hub and its DR hub, can list the same file.

items.title: File name
items.text: fleet/<cluster>.yaml, where <cluster> is the ManagedCluster name exactly (oc get managedclusters). A .yml file, a different case or a typo enrolls nothing, and CI doesn't fail it. Keep cluster names within the 30-character budget, because Policy names are built from them. A hub's file is fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml (Hub file).

items.title: Keys
items.text:
Two ApplicationSets on the hub read fleet files (ApplicationSets). policystack creates the element Applications that configure a running cluster and reads revision, valueFiles, version and channel. policystack-lifecycle builds and destroys clusters and reads every key, but only in files that set hub.

Key Required Effect revision Yes Branch, tag or SHA that every Application of the cluster renders from (Revision). valueFiles No Values layers, as paths relative to values/ (environments/prod.yaml, not values/environments/prod.yaml), lowest precedence first. values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml is added after them automatically. An entry missing at the revision is skipped silently by Argo CD, which is why CI fails it (POLICY052). hub No hubName of the hub that builds the cluster. Without it, import the cluster yourself. Removing it, with state and install, abandons a built cluster (Abandon). state No present (default) or absent. absent destroys the cluster (Destroy). Requires hub. install No What to build: engine, platform, nodes (Install keys). Values layers can set install too, for keys shared by many clusters; the fleet file's install is applied above all of them. Elements ignore it. Requires hub. version With hub OpenShift release, x.y.z. With hub it picks the release the hub installs; leaving it out fails the lifecycle-<cluster> render with version is required. After install, and on every imported cluster or hub, a release newer than the running one starts an upgrade: the hub upgrades HyperShift-built clusters, the upgrade element every other cluster, including those built by hive or siteconfig (OpenShift upgrades). channel No Update channel. On HyperShift-built clusters the hub sets HostedCluster spec.channel; everywhere else the upgrade element enforces ClusterVersion spec.channel. Unset, the cluster's channel is left alone.

version and channel are accepted only in fleet files; POLICY034 rejects them in a values layer. That way the clusters a merge upgrades are exactly the fleet files it changes, each one listed in the PR's Render Diff.

hubName exists because every hub's own ManagedCluster is named local-cluster by default (the MultiClusterHub can set localClusterName), so fleet/local-cluster.yaml could not tell hubs apart (The hub).

items.title: What CI rejects
items.text:
POLICY050 checks every fleet file before merge, in your repository's CI and in make -C tools/validator validate (Validator rules). It fails on:

  • a YAML error, an unknown key, or a missing or empty revision;
  • an unquoted value Argo CD would read as a number or boolean (Quote numbers and booleans);
  • a valueFiles entry that is null, listed twice, or not a file under values/;
  • a version that is not x.y.z, or install.version (use the top-level version);
  • an empty hub, version or channel;
  • a hub with no fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml, or a hub that names the cluster itself;
  • state other than present or absent, or an install that is not a map;
  • state or install without hub;
  • hub, state or install in a hub file;
  • a cluster with hub whose name is not a DNS label, since the hub names the HostedCluster after it.

POLICY052 then checks the revision itself (Revision).

items.title: Quote numbers and booleans
items.text:
Warning

Argo CD reads fleet files as YAML 1.1 into untyped values, then templates them as text. revision: 1.10 becomes the number 1.1, revision: 20261003 becomes 2.0261003e+07, revision: on becomes true. Each names a ref that doesn't exist, which stops Application generation (Revision). Write "1.10", "20261003", "on". The same applies to version: version: 4.20 is the number 4.2. POLICY050 catches every case.

items.title: Revision
items.text:
revision is a branch (slashes work, release/2026-11), a tag, HEAD (the default branch), or a commit SHA: all 40 characters, or at least the first 7, in lowercase. Argo CD tries a full SHA first, then a branch or tag of that name, then an abbreviated SHA. If a branch and a tag share a name, which one Argo CD picks is undefined, so never reuse a name. A branch follows every push to it; a tag or SHA changes only when you edit revision. Which to use and how to promote between them: Rolling out changes.

POLICY052 fails a PR when the revision doesn't resolve, or when its commit lacks what the file uses:

fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: v1.4.0  # (1)!
hub: acm-dc1      # (2)!
version: 4.20.8   # (3)!
  1. v1.4.0 must contain stack/ and every valueFiles entry. A typo, or a branch such as gh-pages, fails.
  2. The commit must contain lifecycle/, the chart that builds clusters. CI checks for lifecycle/converters/_hypershift/, present in every revision that can build clusters, whatever the engine.
  3. The commit must contain the upgrade element (stack/upgrade). It ships enabled. If a layer sets stack.upgrade.enabled: false, version and channel do nothing on any cluster except HyperShift-built ones, whose upgrades the hub runs.

Two rules read oddly at first:

  • A pin to the PR's base branch is checked against the merge commit. In a PR to main, revision: main resolves to what main will be after the merge. A PR that adds both a fleet file and the values it lists therefore passes.
  • A values/clusters/<name>.yaml that no fleet/<name>.yaml or fleet/hubs/<name>.yaml reads is a warning, not an error. For a tag-pinned cluster, values/clusters/<name>.yaml is merged and tagged before the fleet PR that pins that tag, so for a while no fleet file reads it (First cluster). Once your repository has its first fleet file, every file in values/clusters/ that no fleet file reads shows this warning. Delete those you don't use.

items.title: When a revision breaks
items.text:
CI checks the pin only at merge. A branch deleted later, including a PR branch GitHub deletes on merge, stops Application generation for the whole hub (One bad fleet file stops the hub). Pin tags, SHAs or protected branches.

# the generation error, if any
oc get applicationset policystack policystack-lifecycle -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.status.conditions[?(@.type=="ErrorOccurred")].message}{"\n"}{end}'

items.title: Hub file
items.text:
A hub reads fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml, never fleet/<cluster>.yaml. It may not set hub, state or install: a hub cannot build itself, and policystack-lifecycle never reads fleet/hubs/.

A managed hub imported into a Global Hub in default mode has no local-cluster of its own. The global hub's policystack ApplicationSet reads fleet/hubs/<cluster>.yaml for it, where <cluster> is the managed hub's ManagedCluster name on the global hub (Global Hub).

Files in any other subdirectory, such as fleet/prod/edge-1.yaml, are read by nothing, and CI doesn't flag them.

items.title: Labels
items.text:
PolicyStack reads five labels and ignores every other. The ApplicationSets read them from the cluster's Argo CD Secret in openshift-gitops, which ACM's GitOpsCluster creates from the ManagedCluster; the Placement reads name from the ManagedCluster itself. You only ever set the last one.

Label Set by Effect clusterID ACM Selects the cluster's Argo CD Secret. A cluster without it gets no Applications. local-cluster ACM, on the hub Switches to the hub file (Hub file) and uses hubName instead of the cluster name for the Application names and the values/clusters/ file. The Placement still selects the ManagedCluster by its real name. name ACM The Placement selects the cluster by it (Placement). apps.open-cluster-management.io/cluster-name ACM GitOpsCluster, on the Secret only Matches hub to a managed hub imported into a Global Hub in default mode (Global Hub). global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode You, when importing a managed hub into a Global Hub default switches that hub to fleet/hubs/<cluster>.yaml (Global Hub).

PolicyStack installs no RBAC around these labels. Anyone who can label ManagedClusters or edit Secrets in openshift-gitops can change what a cluster runs, for example by adding local-cluster to a spoke so it reads the hub's file. Keep those rights to hub admins. Who may change fleet/ itself is set in your repository (Protect the repository).

items.title: Install chart
items.text:
The install chart is the only part of PolicyStack you install by hand, once per hub (Install PolicyStack). It installs no elements. It creates the two ApplicationSets that turn fleet files into Applications, the pstack namespace the Policies live in, the objects that give the ApplicationSets their list of clusters, and the RBAC Argo CD needs to write ACM policy objects. Everything after it comes from Git.

ApplicationSets explains how the objects work together.

Two charts under install/

install/operators is a separate chart, rendered once to install ACM and OpenShift GitOps on a new hub (Install the operators). It is not part of the policystack release.

items.title: Values
items.text:
Value Required Set with What it does Changing it later gitRepo Yes --set Clone URL of your repository, such as https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git. The repoURL of both ApplicationSets' git generators and of every Application. For a private repository it must equal the url of the Argo CD repository Secret that holds its credentials (Private repository). helm upgrade policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops --reset-then-reuse-values --set gitRepo=<url> re-points every Application at once, so the new repo needs the same fleet files and every pinned revision. hubName Yes --set This hub's name in PolicyStack: picks fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml and values/clusters/<hubName>.yaml, names the hub's Applications <element>-<hubName>, and selects the fleet files whose hub key names this hub as the builder (Fleet keys, The hub). Use a lowercase DNS label of at most 30 characters, because it ends up in Policy names (Naming limits). Unique per active hub reading the repo; a DR hub takes over the old hub's name. Renames and recreates every hub Application and its Policies, and drops lifecycle Applications for hub: <old> (Changing hubName). policyNamespace Default pstack install/values.yaml Namespace the chart creates and binds the global set into. Elements read their own copy from the root values.yaml. Leave at pstack. Changing it, even in both files, renames every Policy, so all are deleted and recreated (Removal and pruning). If install/values.yaml and the root values.yaml differ, elements render into a namespace this chart did not create or bind: their Applications fail to sync or their Placements select nothing. CI rule POLICY071 compares the two files; a --set policyNamespace at install bypasses it.

The chart only checks that gitRepo and hubName are set. A hubName with uppercase letters or _ installs, but the hub's Applications are never created: policystack shows an ErrorOccurred condition with the API server's invalid-name message. Fix it with helm upgrade policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops --reset-then-reuse-values --set hubName=<valid> and name the hub's files to match.

Both values are stored in the Helm release. Read them back with helm get values policystack -n openshift-gitops.

items.title: Objects
items.text:
Three different objects are called global: ACM's built-in ManagedClusterSet that contains every ManagedCluster, and this chart's ManagedClusterSetBindings and Placement that use it. The release and the first ApplicationSet are both named policystack.

Object Name Namespace Why it exists ApplicationSet policystack openshift-gitops One Application per element per cluster that has a fleet file and a clusterID label (policystack). ApplicationSet policystack-lifecycle openshift-gitops One Application per cluster this hub builds, from fleet files with hub: <hubName> (Lifecycle generator). Namespace pstack (policyNamespace) Holds every Policy, PolicySet, Placement and PlacementBinding the Applications render. ManagedClusterSetBinding global openshift-gitops, pstack A Placement can only select clusters from sets bound into its own namespace. openshift-gitops is for the Placement below; pstack for every element Placement. Placement global openshift-gitops Selects every cluster for the GitOpsCluster. Tolerates unreachable and unavailable, so a cluster that loses contact keeps its Argo CD secret, and with it its Applications and Policies (Cluster secrets). GitOpsCluster argo-acm-importer-global openshift-gitops Creates an Argo CD cluster secret, with the ManagedCluster's labels, for each cluster the Placement selects. The secrets are only the ApplicationSets' list of clusters: argoServer.cluster is notused, a placeholder for a required field nothing reads, and every Application deploys to the hub. ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding openshift-gitops-policy-admin The OpenShift GitOps application controller cannot create or change ACM policy objects. Grants it get, list, watch, create, update, patch and delete on policies, configurationpolicies, certificatepolicies, operatorpolicies, policysets, placementbindings, placementrules, placements, placementdecisions and the two status subresources, the role from ACM's "Policy definitions with GitOps". Bound only to openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller, which is why PolicyStack needs the default Argo CD instance.

AppProject default

Every generated Application uses the default AppProject, which the chart does not create. OpenShift GitOps ships it unrestricted. If yours is restricted, allow your repository's URL as a source and https://kubernetes.default.svc with namespaces open-cluster-management and pstack as destinations, or every Application shows an InvalidSpecError saying the source repository or destination is not permitted in project default.

items.title: Backup and restore
items.text:
ACM's cluster backup (the hub backup and restore operator) continuously restores the active hub's objects onto a passive DR hub. The ApplicationSets, their Applications, the Placement and the GitOpsCluster carry velero.io/exclude-from-backup: "true" so the passive hub doesn't start PolicyStack while the active hub still runs: a restored policystack-lifecycle would build the active hub's clusters a second time. CI rule POLICY071 fails if the label goes missing.

The namespace, bindings and RBAC are not excluded and are harmless if restored. After a takeover, run helm install on the new hub with the hubName of the hub it replaces (Hub disaster recovery).

items.title: Uninstall
items.text: Every object carries helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so helm uninstall policystack -n openshift-gitops removes only the release record and PolicyStack keeps running. Deleting the ApplicationSets deletes every Application and every Policy they rendered, and abandons the clusters this hub built: they keep running, unmanaged (Destroy and abandon). Neither helm uninstall nor a failed helm upgrade can delete them. Teardown is a deliberate oc delete (Teardown).

items.title: Preview and upgrade
items.text:
helm template policystack ./install --set hubName=acm-dc1 --set gitRepo=https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git

Run from the root of your repository. A merged change under install/, which only a framework update brings, does nothing until you run helm upgrade on the hub. Then it reaches every cluster on that hub at once, because the ApplicationSets are not pinned to any fleet file's revision. Upgrade as in Upgrading PolicyStack.

items.title: Lifecycle keys
items.text:
Every install key the lifecycle/ chart reads, the objects it renders from them, the steps of its Policies, and what to do when a build fails. Read Cluster lifecycle first for the model; Building clusters has complete examples. hub, state, version and channel are in Fleet files.

Every engine and platform is a preview

Lifecycle follows the framework's version, but no engine or platform is stable yet: a framework minor may change their converters, behaviour and defaults not fixed at create, with the steps in its release notes. Their install keys and the names of the objects they create change only in a major (Maturity). Pin clusters the hub builds to tags.

How to read this page:

  • hypershift keys sit directly under install (install.platform, install.nodePools). hive and siteconfig keys sit under install.hive and install.siteconfig, so install.hive.platform is a different key from install.platform. Any values layer can set install; the fleet file's install wins.
  • The chart's schema rejects unknown keys, and rejects a non-empty hive or siteconfig block unless engine selects it. It does not reject hypershift keys under another engine: hive and siteconfig ignore them.
  • Fixed at create means the engine's API rejects later changes. Changing the key never rebuilds the cluster: present-cluster-<cluster> goes NonCompliant until you revert it (Immutable fields).
  • Fails the render means Helm stops on a schema error, required or fail. Application lifecycle-<cluster> shows the message as a ComparisonError and nothing on the hub changes. A step that fails does so later, when ACM evaluates it on the hub: that step goes NonCompliant with the message, and the steps after it stay Pending (Troubleshooting).

items.title: Install keys
items.text:
Defaults are in lifecycle/values.yaml.

Key Default Notes engine hypershift hypershift, hive or siteconfig (Pick an engine). Never change it on a live cluster: the hub can build a second cluster (Changing engine). Destroy first. credential.namespace, .name required Opaque hub Secret you create by hand, in any namespace; an ACM console credential (Infrastructure > Credentials) of the matching type has these data keys. Creation commands: Building clusters. Keys: pullSecret, ssh-publickey, and for hive the cloud keys (AWS aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key; GCP osServiceAccount.json; Azure osServicePrincipal.json; vSphere username, password, cacertificate). baseDomain "" Required except on KubeVirt, which uses the hub's ingress domain. Fixed at create. releaseRepository quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release Image is <releaseRepository>:<version>-multi, -x86_64 on siteconfig. Point at a mirror when disconnected. manifests [] Extra hub objects with apiVersion, kind, metadata, applied by the manifests step before the cluster. Applied as musthave with no ownership check, so an existing object of the same name is patched. cleanup deletes every object listed at destroy time, one that existed before included. Removing an entry stops managing the object but never deletes it. ACM templates inside entries resolve on the hub.

Keep the credential for the cluster's life

The credentials step re-reads it on every evaluation and copies it into per-cluster Secrets. If it is deleted, credentials fails and every later step stops, so version bumps and NodePool changes no longer apply. Lifecycle never deletes it.

hypershifthivesiteconfig Key Default Notes platform required KubeVirt, Agent or None. No default: without it the render fails with install.platform is required. Fixed at create. namespace clusters HostedCluster, NodePools and copied Secrets. The control plane runs in <namespace>-<cluster>. agentNamespace "" Namespace of the InfraEnv and Agents you created. Required on Agent. services APIServer: LoadBalancer, others Route Service name to servicePublishingStrategy. APIServer, OAuthServer, Konnectivity, Ignition: HyperShift needs all four. Maps merge, so setting one keeps the defaults for the others. Fixed at create. hostedCluster {} metadata and spec merged over the generated HostedCluster: your values win, maps merge, lists replace. spec.release is ignored. Removing a field later does not remove it from the live object. metadata.labels are copied to the ManagedCluster once, at creation; later changes are not, so edit the ManagedCluster directly. nodePools {} Pool name to NodePool spec, without a spec: wrapper, merged over the generated spec. release is ignored. Named <cluster>-<pool>. No replicas means 0. Removing a pool stops managing it; delete the NodePool by hand (Removing a NodePool).

hcp-agent reads environments/prod.yaml, datacenters/dc1.yaml, platforms/agent.yaml, values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml and its fleet file. PolicyStack ships no fleet/; the example fleet file is the header comment of values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml, with the nodePools of the Agent example in Building clusters. The merged install, trimmed:

install:
  platform: Agent                    # (1)!
  agentNamespace: hardware-inventory
  credential:
    namespace: hcp-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  baseDomain: dc1.example.com        # (2)!
  services:                          # (3)!
    APIServer:
      type: LoadBalancer
      loadBalancer:
        hostname: api-int-hcp-agent.dc1.example.com
    OAuthServer:
      type: Route
      route:
        hostname: oauth-hcp-agent.dc1.example.com
    Konnectivity: ...
    Ignition: ...
  hostedCluster:                     # (4)!
    spec:
      kubeAPIServerDNSName: api-hcp-agent.dc1.example.com
  nodePools:
    workers:                         # (5)!
      replicas: 2
      platform:
        agent:
          agentLabelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              example.com/cluster: hcp-agent
  manifests:
    - apiVersion: metallb.io/v1beta1 # (6)!
      kind: IPAddressPool
      metadata:
        name: hcp-agent-apiserver
        namespace: metallb-system
      spec:
        addresses:
          - 10.20.9.13/32
  1. platform, agentNamespace and credential come from platforms/agent.yaml.
  2. From datacenters/dc1.yaml, shared by every cluster in dc1.
  3. From values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml, which sets all four services to add hostnames. A layer that set only APIServer would keep the default Route for the other three.
  4. Also from values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml, with a configuration.apiServer serving certificate not shown.
  5. From the fleet file. NodePool hcp-agent-workers. A pool without agentLabelSelector claims any free Agent in agentNamespace.
  6. From values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml, with an L2Advertisement and a cert-manager Certificate not shown. The manifests step creates it before the HostedCluster, so MetalLB has the address when the kube-apiserver Service asks for one.
Key Default Notes hive.platform required Exactly one of aws, gcp, azure, vsphere, as in the installer's install-config. Needs region; GCP adds projectID, Azure baseDomainResourceGroupName. region, baseDomainResourceGroupName and cloudName also go to the ClusterDeployment. vSphere: needs vcenters and failureDomains, refuses user/password; every vcenters entry gets the credential's login, in the install-config only. Fixed at create. hive.installConfig {} Merged under the generated install-config: the chart's apiVersion, metadata.name, baseDomain and platform win over the same keys here. pullSecret is left out; Hive adds it from pullSecretRef. sshKey defaults to the credential's ssh-publickey. Hive drops fields its installer does not know. Changes after create reach the install-config Secret, not the cluster. hive.clusterDeployment {} metadata and spec merged over the generated ClusterDeployment; your values win. spec.provisioning.releaseImage is ignored. 
# values/platforms/aws.yaml, trimmed
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: aws                       # (1)!
  hive:
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          aws:
            type: m6i.xlarge
      networking:
        networkType: OVNKubernetes

# fleet/ocp-aws.yaml
install:
  baseDomain: aws.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      aws:
        region: us-east-2           # (2)!
  1. Holds pullSecret, ssh-publickey, aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key.
  2. Goes to both the install-config and the ClusterDeployment.
Key Default Notes siteconfig.templates ai ai (assisted installer) or ibi (image-based, single node). ibi needs the host preinstalled from a seed image at version beforehand, outside PolicyStack, and the MCE image-based-install-operator component enabled; no key here sets the seed (Building clusters). Fixed at create. siteconfig.templateNamespace open-cluster-management Namespace of the stock <templates>-cluster-templates-v1 and <templates>-node-templates-v1 ConfigMaps. siteconfig.bmcCredential.namespace, .name required Hub Secret with username and password, copied to <cluster>-bmc. credentials fails on an empty username or password. Keep it for the cluster's life, as for credential. siteconfig.machineNetwork Node subnets. Required with ai and one master. siteconfig.apiVIPs, .ingressVIPs Required with more than one master, forbidden with one. Up to 2 (dual-stack), the same number in each. siteconfig.clusterNetwork installer default {cidr, hostPrefix} list. siteconfig.serviceNetwork installer default Subnets. siteconfig.ntpSources Extra NTP sources. siteconfig.proxy httpProxy and/or httpsProxy, noProxy. siteconfig.extraManifests ConfigMap names in namespace <cluster>, from install.manifests. siteconfig.fips false true installs in FIPS mode. ai only. siteconfig.cpuPartitioning false true installs with workload partitioning. ai only. Enable partitioning on the cluster for its PerformanceProfile. siteconfig.nodes required hostName to the keys below. Layers merge per host. Node key Default Notes bmcAddress required redfish-, idrac- or ilo5-virtualmedia, with optional +http/+https; ilo4-virtualmedia, optional +https. bootMACAddress required Quote it: YAML 1.1 tools read some all-digit MACs as base-60 numbers. role master master, worker or arbiter. rootDeviceHints BareMetalHost hints. deviceName takes /dev/ or /dev/disk/by-path/ only. network Static install network: interfaces (NIC name to MAC) and config (nmstate). Install only; afterwards change node networking with the nmstate element on the cluster. remove true on a worker scales it in. The schema requires role: worker on the same node, set explicitly. Not allowed with ibi.

All of it is fixed at create; afterwards you can only add and remove workers. ai takes 1 or 3 masters, or 2 or more with an arbiter (4.19+). ibi takes one node and no VIPs, clusterNetwork, serviceNetwork, fips or cpuPartitioning: the seed image fixes them. Anything else fails the render, for example install.siteconfig.nodes: 2 masters; need 1, 3, or 2 or more with an arbiter.

FIPS

The hub's nodes must run in FIPS mode: assisted-service runs the installer there, and the installer refuses FIPS on a non-FIPS host. The ssh-publickey must be RSA or ECDSA, as FIPS mode disables ed25519. present-cluster-<cluster> fails before create on either.

# values/platforms/baremetal.yaml
install:
  engine: siteconfig
  credential:
    namespace: bm-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  siteconfig:
    bmcCredential:
      namespace: bm-credentials
      name: bmc

# fleet/sno-edge.yaml
install:
  siteconfig:
    machineNetwork: [10.20.30.0/24]
    nodes:
      sno-edge.dc1.example.com:     # (1)!
        bmcAddress: redfish-virtualmedia://10.20.0.11/redfish/v1/Systems/1
        bootMACAddress: "00:11:22:33:44:55"
  1. The key becomes hostName.

items.title: Generated objects
items.text:
What the credentials and cluster steps create. <cluster> is the fleet file name. Everything not listed uses the operator's defaults; override it in hostedCluster or hive.clusterDeployment. siteconfig takes only the keys above. Every root object, and the ManagedCluster on hive and siteconfig, carries the ownership marker.

hypershifthivesiteconfig Object Content Secrets <cluster>-pull-secret, <cluster>-ssh-key Copied from the credential into namespace. Secret <cluster>-etcd-encryption-key Agent and None only; HyperShift creates its own on KubeVirt. HostedCluster <namespace>/<cluster> Release image, pullSecret, sshKey, platform, services, channel and dns.baseDomain when set. Agent adds agentNamespace. Agent and None add secretEncryption with the etcd key. NodePool <namespace>/<cluster>-<pool> clusterName, release image, platform, management.upgradeType (Replace on KubeVirt, else InPlace).

etcd encryption key

Generated once, while neither the key nor the HostedCluster exists. A deleted key is never regenerated: a new key cannot decrypt etcd. Restore it from backup.

Rendered for the hcp-agent values above, trimmed 
apiVersion: hypershift.openshift.io/v1beta1
kind: HostedCluster
metadata:
  name: hcp-agent
  namespace: clusters
  annotations:
    lifecycle.policystk.io/hub: acm-dc1
spec:
  channel: stable-4.20
  dns:
    baseDomain: dc1.example.com
  kubeAPIServerDNSName: api-hcp-agent.dc1.example.com
  platform:
    type: Agent
    agent:
      agentNamespace: hardware-inventory
  pullSecret:
    name: hcp-agent-pull-secret
  sshKey:
    name: hcp-agent-ssh-key
  secretEncryption:
    type: aescbc
    aescbc:
      activeKey:
        name: hcp-agent-etcd-encryption-key
  services:
    - service: APIServer
      servicePublishingStrategy:
        type: LoadBalancer
        loadBalancer:
          hostname: api-int-hcp-agent.dc1.example.com
    # Ignition, Konnectivity, OAuthServer: Route with their hostnames
  release:
    image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.20.8-multi  # (1)!
---
apiVersion: hypershift.openshift.io/v1beta1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: hcp-agent-workers
  namespace: clusters
spec:
  clusterName: hcp-agent
  management:
    upgradeType: InPlace
  platform:
    type: Agent
    agent:
      agentLabelSelector:
        matchLabels:
          example.com/cluster: hcp-agent
  replicas: 2
  release:
    image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.20.8-multi
  1. Set from version when allowed: at once without channel, with channel once HyperShift lists it in availableUpdates, never a downgrade. Otherwise the live image stays (Upgrades).
Object Content Namespace <cluster> Holds everything below except the ManagedCluster. Secret <cluster>-pull-secret Copied from the credential. Secret <cluster>-creds Only the cloud keys Hive reads, copied from the credential. Secret <cluster>-certs vSphere: .cacert from cacertificate. Secret <cluster>-install-config install-config.yaml built from hive.installConfig and hive.platform. vSphere: the only place the vCenter login goes. ClusterDeployment <cluster>/<cluster> baseDomain, clusterName, platform with credentialsSecretRef <cluster>-creds, pullSecretRef, installConfigSecretRef, release image, installAttemptsLimit: 1 (a failed install is not retried). vSphere: infrastructure is hive.platform.vsphere with a blank login, plus certificatesSecretRef <cluster>-certs. ManagedCluster <cluster>, KlusterletAddonConfig Every add-on on. Object Content Namespace <cluster>, Secrets <cluster>-pull-secret, <cluster>-bmc Copied from the credential and bmcCredential. ClusterImageSet lifecycle-<cluster> The release image. ClusterInstance <cluster>/<cluster> The keys above, plus clusterName, baseDomain, pullSecretRef, sshPublicKey, templates, clusterImageSetNameRef, per node hostName, bmcCredentialsName <cluster>-bmc and node templates. clusterType follows the masters: 1 is SNO, an arbiter HighlyAvailableArbiter, else HighlyAvailable. fips becomes installConfigOverrides: '{"fips":true}', cpuPartitioning cpuPartitioningMode: AllNodes. SiteConfig defaults bootMode: UEFI, automatedCleaningMode: disabled. KlusterletAddonConfig Every add-on on (Day-2 handoff).

Three fields are read back from the live objects instead of from your values: the ClusterDeployment's spec.provisioning.releaseImage (hive), and the ClusterImageSet's releaseImage and the ClusterInstance's sshPublicKey (siteconfig). Hive rejects release image changes and SiteConfig most spec changes, so a version bump or a new ssh-publickey never reaches them, and a hand edit to the image set is kept. Those clusters upgrade through upgrade. Pull secret, cloud keys and BMC login are not read back: credentials re-copies them on every evaluation.

items.title: Policy chains
items.text:
The steps of present-lifecycle-<cluster> and absent-lifecycle-<cluster> per engine. Why they are chained and gated: The step chain. Each template is named <state>-<step>-<cluster>, e.g. present-guard-hcp-kubevirt, and waits for the one before it to be Compliant.

Mode column: enforce creates or patches (musthave), or deletes with mustnothave. InformOnly only reports, even though the Policy is enforce; with mustnothave it is Compliant once the object is gone. The hypershift and siteconfig ready gates, while unsatisfied, put a mustnothave on the object they wait for, only to name it in the message; nothing is deleted. hive ready is a musthave on spec.installed: true.

present-lifecycle-<cluster>:

Template Mode hypershift hive siteconfig guard InformOnly NonCompliant, naming the object, while the ownership check finds a foreign one. Stops the chain. same same credentials enforce Namespace install.namespace, <cluster>-pull-secret, <cluster>-ssh-key, etcd key on Agent/None Namespace <cluster>, -pull-secret, -creds, -install-config, -certs on vSphere Namespace <cluster>, -pull-secret, -bmc. Fails on an empty BMC username or password. manifests enforce install.manifests same same cluster enforce HostedCluster, NodePools ClusterDeployment, ManagedCluster, KlusterletAddonConfig ClusterImageSet, ClusterInstance, KlusterletAddonConfig ready InformOnly The HostedCluster's desired version and newest Completed version both equal version, and every NodePool reports version spec.installed: true Provisioned True and every host joined (Agent stage Done) or removed. Names the pending host's BareMetalHost while it exists, otherwise the ClusterInstance.

absent-lifecycle-<cluster>:

Template Mode hypershift hive siteconfig guard InformOnly Same check same same detach enforce mustnothave Deletes the ManagedCluster while the cluster is up, so the klusterlet cleans up same none: SiteConfig would re-create it detached InformOnly mustnothave Waits for the ManagedCluster to go same none destroy enforce mustnothave Deletes the HostedCluster; HyperShift deletes the NodePools and control plane Deletes the ClusterDeployment; Hive deprovisions with <cluster>-creds (and -certs on vSphere) Deletes the ClusterInstance; SiteConfig deletes what it rendered: BareMetalHosts, then ManagedCluster destroyed InformOnly mustnothave Waits for the HostedCluster to go Waits for deprovision Waits for the ClusterInstance to go cleanup enforce mustnothave Copied secrets, etcd key, install.manifests Namespace <cluster>, install.manifests Namespace <cluster>, ClusterImageSet, install.manifests

Create templates are musthave: only the fields the template lists are compared, so fields HyperShift or Hive fill in never cause a fight, and nothing is ever removed. The ClusterInstance alone is mustonlyhave with metadataComplianceType: musthave: musthave matches list items by name, which ClusterInstance nodes lack, so a changed node would be appended as a duplicate and a node could never be dropped. metadataComplianceType keeps the labels and annotations SiteConfig adds.

items.title: Immutable fields
items.text:
The engines reject changes to these, among others:

Object Immutable HostedCluster services, platform, networking, etcd, issuerURL, controllerAvailabilityPolicy, fips, dns.baseDomain once set. secretEncryption cannot be removed. NodePool clusterName, platform.type, arch, management.upgradeType ClusterDeployment Everything but installAttemptsLimit, powerState, preserveOnDelete and a few others. hive.installConfig changes reach the Secret, not the cluster. On vSphere all of hive.platform.vsphere. ClusterInstance Everything until the install completes. After: extraAnnotations, extraLabels, suppressedManifests, pruneManifests, clusterImageSetNameRef, and adding or removing workers. The chart never changes clusterImageSetNameRef.

A change to any of these is denied and blocks every other change to that object (Immutable fields). Revert the value.

  • NodePool upgradeType or arch: add a new pool, remove the old one.
  • Any siteconfig key on a live cluster, including a field of an existing worker: unauthorized changes in immutable fields (cluster keys) or unauthorized change to … (host keys). Only adding and removing workers is allowed.
  • Any ClusterInstance spec edit before the install completes: spec update not allowed during provisioning or cluster reinstalls. The step retries after the install, but SiteConfig then accepts only the changes listed in the table, so anything else is denied again as immutable. Revert it, or destroy and build again. A new worker never hits this: the chart holds it back until the install completes.
  • Failed SiteConfig install: destroy, then build again with the fix (Destroy).

ClusterInstance is mustonlyhave

A render change on an installed cluster is denied on every evaluation. A hand-set spec.reinstall keeps present-cluster-<cluster> NonCompliant the same way, and a SiteConfig webhook outage turns installed clusters NonCompliant until it returns (why).

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Check the Application first for render errors (missing version, credential or required key), then the Policy's steps. Read the first step that is not Compliant; the ones after it are Pending.

oc get applications.argoproj.io lifecycle-<cluster> -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'
oc get policy present-lifecycle-<cluster> -n pstack                                  # overall Compliant/NonCompliant
oc get policy pstack.present-lifecycle-<cluster> -n local-cluster -o jsonpath='{range .status.details[*]}{.templateMeta.name}{": "}{.history[0].message}{"\n"}{end}'   # each step's compliance and message
oc get configurationpolicy -n local-cluster present-<step>-<cluster> -o yaml         # one step in full

The steps run in the hub's own cluster namespace, local-cluster; under a default-mode Global Hub, in the managed hub's namespace on that hub (Global Hub).

Symptom Cause Fix No lifecycle-<cluster> Application after ~6 min Fleet file not on the default branch; hub differs from the hub's hubName; hub has no local-cluster; ApplicationSet generation error oc get applicationset policystack-lifecycle -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'; see Fleet files. guard: …: not built by lifecycle (no lifecycle.policystk.io/hub annotation); refusing to build it (to detach it or to destroy it when absent). Other steps: <Kind> <cluster> was not built by lifecycle (no lifecycle.policystk.io/hub annotation); refusing Imported, or built by hand or the console. Usually hub was added to an imported cluster's fleet file. Remove hub, state and install from the fleet file. Lifecycle never adopts a cluster it did not build (Ownership). present-credentials NonCompliant, template error Credential Secret missing Create it. Without pullSecret the API rejects the pull secret. Cluster has no SSH key, no error ssh-publickey missing from the credential Add it. hive/siteconfig: present-credentials-<cluster> NonCompliant: because it is being terminated Namespace <cluster> from the last destroy is still terminating Wait until oc get ns <cluster> returns NotFound. present-cluster-<cluster> NonCompliant with an API or webhook denial A fixed-at-create key changed Revert it. Two clusters with the same name after changing engine Ownership check missed the switch Destroy the new one; never change engine without destroying first (Changing engine). hypershift cluster built but no Day-2 Applications autoImportDisabled in AddOnDeploymentConfig hypershift-addon-deploy-config Remove it, or import by hand. Hive: install failed

present-ready stays NonCompliant, ClusterDeployment shows ProvisionStopped. Read the installer log:

oc logs -n <cluster> -l hive.openshift.io/install=true -c installer

Hive does not retry (installAttemptsLimit: 1), and provisioning fields are immutable, so fixed values never reach this ClusterDeployment. Fix the values, destroy and build again.

RequirementsMet False with InstallConfigValidationFailed: the install-config and ClusterDeployment regions differ, through hive.clusterDeployment or an edit of hive.platform during install. Revert it.

A cloud key missing from the credential is copied as an empty value and fails the install.

Hive: vSphere credentials rejected

ClusterDeployment AuthenticationFailure True: the hub could not log in to vCenter with <cluster>-creds and <cluster>-certs. Check for a wrong login, a trailing newline, a cacertificate that is not PEM, vCenter on a port other than 443, or no route from the hub. Right after create it can be brief while the trust bundle fills.

RequirementsMet False, "install config does not contain username/password": the credential is missing username or password.

cluster NonCompliant with must specify vSphere vCenter: the hub's Hive predates zonal vSphere support. Upgrade MCE.

Hive: deprovision stuck

absent-destroyed stays NonCompliant; ClusterDeployment shows DeprovisionLaunchError, or the ClusterDeprovision AuthenticationFailure. Fix the keys in <cluster>-creds (or <cluster>-certs on vSphere) directly: the absent Policy no longer copies the credential.

absent-destroy-<cluster> NonCompliant with a webhook denial mentioning protected delete (HiveConfig deleteProtection: enabled):

oc annotate clusterdeployment <cluster> -n <cluster> hive.openshift.io/protected-delete-
SiteConfig: rejected or failed

present-cluster shows a webhook denial, or the ClusterInstance shows Provisioned False:

oc get clusterinstance <cluster> -n <cluster> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'

Check the AgentClusterInstall too. Destroy, fix, build again. A wrong ref, like templateNamespace, can be fixed by creating the missing object. For a hub-side problem, check Policy ready-cim-<hubName> from the cim element, which reports whether the hub's provisioning services run: oc get policy -n pstack ready-cim-<hubName>.

SiteConfig: cluster never imported

The hub cannot resolve api.<cluster>.<baseDomain>. Add the DNS record where the hub resolves it.

SiteConfig: deletion paused

The ClusterInstance has clusterinstance.siteconfig.open-cluster-management.io/paused: a rendered object (usually a BareMetalHost or the ManagedCluster) was not gone within 30 minutes. Fix what holds it, then remove the annotation.

HyperShift: ManagedCluster stuck Terminating

absent-detached stays NonCompliant. A hosted cluster's klusterlet runs on the hub in hosted mode, as Klusterlet klusterlet-<cluster>, and its cleanup waits for the guest to answer; ACM gives up after 5 minutes unreachable. Check:

oc get klusterlet klusterlet-<cluster> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.finalizers}'

If it waits on operator.open-cluster-management.io/klusterlet-hosted-cleanup and the guest will not answer, remove that finalizer.

HyperShift Agent: Machines stuck Deleting (destroy or NodePool scale-down)

Machines in the control-plane namespace <namespace>-<cluster> (clusters-<cluster> by default) stay Deleting, PreTerminateDeleteHookSucceeded reports WaitingExternalHook. Remove the hook:

for m in $(oc get machines.cluster.x-k8s.io -n clusters-<cluster> -o name); do
  oc annotate "$m" -n clusters-<cluster> pre-terminate.delete.hook.machine.cluster.x-k8s.io/agentmachine-
done
Agent: stuck reclaiming

After destroy, Agents go to reclaiming while they reboot into discovery. One that cannot ends in UnbindingPendingUserAction: boot it from the discovery ISO by hand. Agents still holding the agent.agent-install.openshift.io/ai-deprovision finalizer block any new cluster that selects them.

items.title: Validator rules
items.text:
Every rule the validator (tools/validator) runs, by ID. You land here from a finding such as error POLICY033 [metallb] ..., in your terminal or as an annotation on a PR line. What the validator does, how to run it and how to read a finding: Validation.

POLICYnnn rules check element sources, values layers, fleet files and the render. RENDER000 means helm template itself failed, so no rule that reads the render ran for that element and cluster: fix it first.

An error fails the run (exit 1) and with it the ci check, which blocks the merge once your repository requires it (Required checks). A warning is reported but passes. Rows marked error/warning say which case is which.

A finding points at the file and line to change. A rule that reads the render points at the values layer that set the field, so a mistake in values/ is reported there, not in the element (Reading the output).

CI runs make -C tools/validator validate, whose flags are fixed in the Makefile, so a PR can't skip a rule. --skip/--only work only when you run the binary by hand. The one opt-out in the repo is POLICY037's: make the template InformOnly (Destructive templates).

Terms the table uses Term Meaning Element A chart under stack/ (How an element is built) Entry A key under policies, policies.<p>.templates or operatorPolicies in an element's values Policy-template, sub-policy A ConfigurationPolicy, OperatorPolicy or CertificatePolicy inside a Policy's spec.policy-templates (ACM policies in brief) Converter A file under an element's converters/, rendered into a template Partial A converter whose file or directory name starts with _: never a template on its own, only rendered when a template's file names it or another chart file reads it Values layer A values file under values/ that a cluster reads: listed in its fleet file's valueFiles, or its own values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml (Values cascade) Cascade The element's values.yaml, then the root values.yaml, then the cluster's layers in order; later files win (Order) Fleet file fleet/<cluster>.yaml or fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml (Fleet files) Replicated name <namespace>.<Policy name>, the name ACM gives the copy of a Policy in the cluster's namespace on the hub InformOnly, gate A template remediationAction ACM never enforces. A gate is an InformOnly template other steps wait on Release <element>-<cluster> (<element>-<hubName> on the hub): the Application and Helm release name. Policy and Placement names end with it PolicySet An ACM object grouping Policies for reporting object-templates-raw A ConfigurationPolicy's objects as one templated string, used when a converter's output starts with an ACM template or a list (Converter shapes) Fixture A made-up fleet file in tools/validator/testdata/clusters the validator renders (Fixtures) Dry run global.remediationAction: inform in a layer: every Policy reports instead of changing (Dry run) Discovery The API kinds the validator's fake cluster serves (ACM templates) Framework add-on The part of ACM's governance add-on on the managed cluster that reads each Policy's templates (ACM policies in brief) Engine, component A lifecycle builder (hypershift, hive, siteconfig), one stack.<engine> block in lifecycle/values.yaml (Cluster lifecycle)

items.title: Rules
items.text: ID Severity What it catches POLICY001 error A rendered Policy or PolicySet whose ACM-replicated name <ns>.<name>-<release> is over 63 characters, or a policy-template (ConfigurationPolicy, OperatorPolicy with its -ns/-status templates, CertificatePolicy) whose metadata.name is. Reads the render, so a values layer that adds an entry is caught, and points at the last cascade file setting the entry, else at its converter POLICY002 error Duplicate policy-template metadata.name WITHIN one element, such as template b-c of policy a and template c of policy a-b. A template only converters/ declares is reported at its converter POLICY003 error Two different elements render a policy-template with the same name. ACM requires template names to be unique across every Policy on a cluster, so template ns-monitoring of policy install in two elements is rejected on-cluster with "Template name must be unique". Covers disabled entries and the -ns/-status templates an operatorPolicy generates POLICY011 error dependency reference that can never be satisfied: unknown dependencies/extraDependencies target, unknown element:, element: on a template kind, waitForOperator naming no operatorPolicies entry, or a target policy policy-library never emits (no template or operator). Disabled entries count, since a layer may turn them on POLICY021 warning A converter policy-library never renders: a .yml file, a .yaml file no template renders (a top-level file no templates.<t>.file names, or converters/<p>/<t>.yaml replaced by the template's own file), or a partial (a path segment starting _) that no file names and no other chart file mentions by name POLICY022 error A converter reads a top-level config key missing from the element's values.yaml, which renders as null: .Config.<key> or .Values.stack.<el>.config.<key>, from $ too, or $v.<key> with $v bound to either. .Config also takes the keys of templates.<t>.config of each template rendering the converter, or of any template in a _ partial no template renders (pulled in with tpl). Only Helm actions count, not escaped ACM templates. Nested keys are not checked POLICY030 error/warning Invalid enum: severity / remediationAction / complianceType / upgradeApproval (None or Automatic), in default, policies.<p> and policies.<p>.templates.<t>, whose remediationAction is only InformOnly. In operatorPolicies entries also: subscription.installPlanApproval set, a versions entry or subscription.startingCSV that is not a valid CSV name (templated entries skipped, comma-separated versions entries split), and a name: key, which is ignored (warning) POLICY031 error/warning values keys policy-library never reads: enable: (element renders nothing) and defaultPolicy: (metadata silently dropped) are errors, default.disabled a warning. Also flags the policy-library 3.x shape (a policies list, configPolicies or toggles: run tools/migrate-4.0.py) and operatorPolicies as a list. A 3.x chart is still rendered (RENDER000) but no other rule runs on it POLICY032 error/warning stack.<el>.operatorPolicies in a values layer: a key the element's values.yaml does not define, a list, or any POLICY030 operator problem. Reported once per layer file POLICY033 error/warning A rendered ConfigurationPolicy's pruneObjectBehavior other than None: an invalid value, an effective remediationAction other than enforce (the Policy's overrides the template's unless it is InformOnly; skipped on a dry run, global.remediationAction), or any dependency (the template's extraDependencies, from waitForOperator, extraDependencies or orderManifests, or the Policy's dependencies), since ACM deletes the template whenever the dependency is unmet. DeleteAll is a warning POLICY034 error Top-level version or channel in a values layer: only the fleet file sets them.
