Reported once per layer file POLICY035 error A key in the root values.yaml or a file under values/ that nothing reads: an unknown top-level or global key, a stack key that names no element, an element key policy-library's schema rejects (reported here at the layer; RENDER000 reports it once per element at its values.yaml), a policies key that names no policy of the element (a policies key, a converters/ directory or install), a templates key that names no template of its policy and sets no file, or a top-level config key missing from the element's values.yaml. Checks every file, used by a fleet file or not POLICY037 error/warning A rendered ConfigurationPolicy object-template that is mustonlyhave or mustnothave on an object OpenShift owns: ConfigMap openshift-config/user-ca-bundle, Secret openshift-config/pull-secret, ClusterVersion version, Proxy and Image cluster (config.openshift.io), or a Namespace starting openshift- or kube-. Enforced, it replaces or deletes platform state. musthave is not covered. Skips an InformOnly template and one annotated validator.policystk.io/allow-destructive: <reason>. object-templates-raw is read with its ACM template actions removed, so every branch counts; raw that is then not YAML is a warning POLICY038 error An operatorPolicies subscription.source (redhat-operators when unset), in an element's values.yaml or a values layer, that is not redhat-operators, certified-operators, community-operators, redhat-marketplace or a global.catalogSources key in any layer. OLM finds no such CatalogSource, so the operator never installs. Templated values are skipped POLICY039 warning A values layer or fleet file sets a key whose description in an element's or lifecycle/'s values.yaml (the comment block directly above it, as tools/doc-generator.py reads it) says Deprecated: use <key>; removed in <version>. The finding names the replacement and the version that removes the key, which keeps working, and known to POLICY035, until then. A Deprecated: note in any other form is reported at the values.yaml. Checks every layer file, used by a fleet file or not POLICY040 error policySets[].policies[] names no policy of the element POLICY050 error Invalid fleet file: YAML error, unknown key, missing or empty revision, revision, hub, state, version, channel or valueFiles entry Argo CD reads as a number or boolean, valueFiles entry that is null, listed twice, or not a file under values/; version that is not x.y.z, install.version; empty hub, version or channel, hub with no hubs/<hub>.yaml, hub naming the cluster itself, hub in a hub file, state other than present/absent, install that is not a map, state or install without hub, or a cluster that sets hub whose name is not a DNS label POLICY051 error Two siteconfig nodes on one hub with the same bootMACAddress or bmcAddress (scheme aside), across fleet files that are not state: absent: two BareMetalHosts would drive one server POLICY052 error/warning A fleet file's revision, resolved in git as Argo CD does (tag, origin branch, then a 5 to 40 character commit SHA; a PR's base branch is the merge commit), that does not resolve or whose commit lacks stack/, lifecycle/converters/_hypershift/ (or the pre-4.0 hypershift/) when hub is set, an upgrade element when version or channel is set, or a valueFiles entry, which Argo CD skips. In a copier copy (a root .copier-answers.yml), also a revision whose .copier-answers.yml records a framework major newer than this branch's, or more than one major older: hubs run this branch's install chart, which renders its own major and the one before. A revision without the file predates the copy and is not checked. A values/clusters/<name>.yaml no fleet file reads is a warning. Needs git history (fetch-depth: 0). make validate runs it on fleet/ only POLICY060 error A chart's Chart.yaml does not take policy-library from this repo: it must have exactly one dependency, policy-library with alias: stack, repository: file://<path to lib/policy-library> and a caret floor (^4.N.0) that lib/policy-library/Chart.yaml version satisfies. Helm reports a wrong repository or floor only as can't get a valid version, and a wrong alias not at all; the finding says what to change POLICY061 error A copier answers file that records the wrong release. The root .copier-answers.yml _commit must be a release tag vX.Y.Z. A stack/<element>/.copier-answers.yml must have element: <element> and a _commit release tag no newer than the root's (semver order, prereleases included) and on the same major: update the framework first, and after a framework major update every element to it. Copied from a branch or commit instead of a tag, copier records git describe output such as v1.2.0-3-gabc1234, which POLICY052 can't read. A directory without an answers file is not checked, and without a root answers file the order is not checked POLICY070 error helm lint non-zero POLICY071 error install/, which each hub runs by hand: helm lint fails, an empty hubName or gitRepo does not fail the install, policyNamespace differs from the root values.yaml, an ApplicationSet (or its Application template), GitOpsCluster or Placement lacks velero.io/exclude-from-backup: "true", or install/operators does not render the ACM and GitOps operators and a MultiClusterHub from the element values, with policy-library's defaults for keys they omit POLICY080 error/warning A rendered object that fails its CRD, checked as the API server would: an unknown field, a value outside an enum such as remediationAction: enforec, or a wrong type. Covers Policy, Placement, PlacementBinding and PolicySet, then each policy-templates[].objectDefinition (ConfigurationPolicy, OperatorPolicy, CertificatePolicy) with InformOnly read as inform, as the framework addon does. Findings name the values entry, without a cluster. A kind with no CRD is one warning per element POLICY081 error An escaped ACM template ACM would fail to resolve, resolved hub then managed on an empty cluster: an undefined function in any branch, a failed call such as index on nil, a hub lookup outside the policy namespace without hubTemplateOptions.serviceAccountName, a kind discovery does not serve, or output with <no value> or an object without apiVersion/kind. A missing object is not a failure. Findings name the sub-policy without its cluster suffix and carry no cluster, so a broken template reports once POLICY082 error A rendered Policy whose every template is a ConfigurationPolicy with no objects (object-templates-raw empty or [], or no object-templates). ACM reports it Compliant without checking anything; policy-library renders [] when a converter renders nothing, as when the map it ranges over is empty. A Policy with only some empty templates passes POLICY090 error Chart.yaml name → camelCase mismatch with single key under stack:. For a chart whose values.schema.json has an install.engine enum (lifecycle/), a stack: key that is not an engine or an engine with no stack: key. Every other check then runs on each engine's component, and each fixture renders the one its install.engine selects POLICY091 error An element name equal to another's, or starting with another's followed by -. Release names join element and cluster with -, so a on cluster b-c and a-b on cluster c would share one Application and its Policies. lifecycle/ takes part, which reserves lifecycle POLICY092 warning stack.<key>.enabled: true for an element whose Chart.yaml sets deprecated: true, in the root values.yaml, a file under values/, or the element's own values.yaml (on for every cluster). The element still renders; a later major removes it. helm template prints the flag only on stderr, which Argo CD discards. Checks every layer file, used by a fleet file or not RENDER000 error helm template failed, or helm dependency update did. A chart whose dependencies were not fetched is not rendered, since Helm would use any charts/ archive of the dependency, whatever its version. Reported once per chart

items.title: Fixing common findings
items.text: Rule Usual cause Fix RENDER000 helm template failed Read the Helm error under the finding. A hint: line names the usual cause: a missing selector (when running the binary by hand, pass the baseline) or a values key the chart reads that no file sets. dependencies not fetched means helm dependency update could not package lib/policy-library: POLICY060 names the Chart.yaml fix POLICY001 A policy or template name too long for a 30-character cluster name Shorten it (Naming limits) POLICY002 Two names collide on one cluster. Also reported across elements: element b with policy x-a and element a-b with policy x both render Policy x-a-b-<cluster>, which POLICY091 doesn't catch Rename one policy or template POLICY003 Two elements ship a template of the same name Rename one. ACM requires template names unique across every Policy on a cluster POLICY021 A file directly under converters/, or an unused partial Move it to converters/<policy>/<template>.yaml, name it in a template's file, or delete it. A _ partial must be named by a file or read by another chart file POLICY022 A converter reads .Config.<key> the element's values.yaml doesn't define Add the key under config: with a default and a comment POLICY030 A misspelled enum, or subscription.installPlanApproval Fix the spelling. ACM's OperatorPolicy rejects installPlanApproval: use upgradeApproval and versions (Operator versions) POLICY033 pruneObjectBehavior on a template that isn't enforced or has a dependency Remove pruneObjectBehavior or the dependency (Removal and pruning) POLICY034 version or channel in a values layer Move it to the cluster's fleet file POLICY035 A typo in values/: a key nothing reads Fix the key the message names POLICY037 mustonlyhave or mustnothave on an object OpenShift owns musthave, or InformOnly (Destructive templates) POLICY038 A subscription.source that is not a default catalog Fix the name, or declare it under global.catalogSources (Disconnected clusters) POLICY039 A layer or fleet file still sets a key an element deprecated Set the replacement the message names instead, before the version it names. A finding at an element's values.yaml is a malformed note: write it as Deprecated: use <key>; removed in <version> (Deprecating a key) POLICY050 A broken fleet file Fix the key the message names. install.version is an error whatever its value: use the top-level version POLICY052 A revision that doesn't resolve, a commit missing what the fleet file uses, or one on a framework major the hubs don't render Push the branch or tag first. The "upgrade element" is stack/upgrade: a fleet file setting version or channel needs a revision that has it. Locally, main means origin/main (flags). A newer major: merge the framework update and upgrade the hubs first. Two or more majors older: move the revision forward (Majors) POLICY060 A Chart.yaml copied from outside stack/, written by hand, or with a floor above lib/policy-library Set what the message names. A floor above the library means the library change this chart needs is missing, or lib/policy-library/Chart.yaml version was not bumped with it (Library changes) POLICY061 copier copy or copier update from a branch or commit instead of a release tag, an element copied into the wrong directory, an element updated past the framework, or an element left on an older major than the framework Rerun it with the right tag: update the framework first, then take the element at the framework's tag. Never edit an answers file by hand (Answers files) POLICY070 helm lint failed on the element with only its own values.yaml, where it is off A chart structure error; render problems are RENDER000 POLICY080 A misspelled field or enum value in a rendered object Fix the field the message names POLICY081 An ACM template that fails on an empty cluster ACM templates POLICY082 An optional piece turned on with an empty input map, so its Policy checks nothing Give it its config input (Profiles) POLICY090 values.yaml has no single stack.<key> matching the chart name in camelCase (user-monitoring → userMonitoring), so policy-library reads a different key and renders nothing Rename the key. The engine part applies only to lifecycle/ POLICY092 A layer turns on an element marked deprecated: true Move to the element that replaces it, then remove enabled: true from the file the finding names

items.title: First cluster
items.text:
Onboard an imported cluster and turn on one element. Onboarding is four hand-offs:

  1. You import the cluster into ACM. The GitOpsCluster from Installation creates an Argo CD cluster secret for it.
  2. You merge fleet/<cluster>.yaml to the default branch. It enrolls the cluster and names the revision and values layers it reads.
  3. The policystack ApplicationSet creates one Application per element for the cluster. Each renders the element's Policies into pstack on the hub.
  4. ACM copies each Policy to the cluster, where ACM's governance add-on (installed at import) applies it and reports compliance.

More: How a change reaches a cluster.

PolicyStack must be installed on the hub. The hub doesn't need its own fleet file for this. The examples use prod-east-1; replace it with your cluster's name.

items.title: Onboard the cluster
items.text:
1. Import the cluster into ACM (Importing a cluster). Use its ManagedCluster name everywhere below. Pick a name of 30 characters or fewer before importing. A ManagedCluster can't be renamed, and with a longer name some replicated Policy names (pstack.<policy>-<element>-<cluster>) exceed 63 characters, which ACM rejects, so those Policies never reach the cluster (Naming limits).

    Once the import finishes, ACM sets the clusterID label, and the cluster gets its Argo CD secret. A cluster without the label gets no Applications and no error. ACM sets clusterID from the OpenShift ClusterVersion once the cluster joins (AVAILABLE True). If it's missing, the import hasn't finished: check the conditions in oc get managedcluster prod-east-1 -o yaml.

    oc get managedcluster prod-east-1 -L clusterID
# NAME          HUB ACCEPTED   ...   AVAILABLE   AGE   CLUSTERID
# prod-east-1   true           ...   True        5m    1b2c3d4e-...
oc get secrets -n openshift-gitops -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster,name=prod-east-1
# one secret

  2. PR the fleet file to the default branch. For this walkthrough, list no layers. Merge once CI passes:

    # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main  # (1)!
    1. Where stack/ and values/ are read. A branch makes the cluster follow every merge to it. A tag or SHA holds it there until you change this line, which is how changes are promoted cluster by cluster (Rolling out changes). Use main for a first or lab cluster.

    The fleet file itself is always read from the default branch, because it says which revision to read everything else at (Fleet files). Name it exactly like the ManagedCluster: a misnamed fleet file matches nothing and reports no error.

    CI rejects an invalid fleet file or a revision missing a listed layer (POLICY050, POLICY052), and Render Diff comments the Policies the merge adds (Protect the repository).

    Adding shared layers

    List layers under valueFiles, lowest precedence first (Values cascade):

    # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml  # (1)!
  - platforms/aws.yaml      # (2)!
    1. A layer you wrote, or copied from upstream's examples (Example files). Upstream's environments/prod.yaml turns elements on and enforces them. Read a layer before you list it.
    2. Picks the AWS variant of the node elements.

    Helm merges the element's values.yaml, the root values.yaml, each listed layer, then values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml. Later files win: maps merge key by key, lists are replaced whole (Merge rules).

    Land the cluster file before the fleet file

    If values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml turns off something a listed layer turns on, it must already be at the revision when the fleet file merges. Otherwise the first render enforces the element, and turning it off afterwards deletes the Policy but not what it changed (What happens on the managed cluster). With remediations from a copy of upstream's environments/prod.yaml, the Samples Operator stays Removed.

    • revision: main: put both files in one PR.
    • Tag or SHA: merge the cluster file to main, tag, then PR the fleet file pinning the new tag.

    A misnamed cluster file is skipped silently (Missing files).

items.title: Check the Applications
items.text:
Within about 6 minutes each directory under stack/ has an Application named <element>-<cluster>. The ApplicationSet lists directories and can't read values, so an element no layer turns on still gets an Application. It renders nothing and shows Synced and Healthy.

oc get applications.argoproj.io -n openshift-gitops | grep prod-east-1  # (1)!
# acm-prod-east-1           Synced        Healthy
# cert-manager-prod-east-1  Synced        Healthy
# ...
  1. ACM installs a second applications kind, so use the full name.
No Applications

Check in order:

  1. The ManagedCluster has the clusterID label and a cluster secret exists (step 1).
  2. fleet/prod-east-1.yaml is on the default branch, named exactly like the ManagedCluster.

  3. The ApplicationSet's error. A YAML error, a missing revision or a revision that doesn't exist stops Application changes for every cluster on the hub (One bad fleet file stops the hub):

    oc get applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="ErrorOccurred")].message}'

items.title: Enable an element
items.text:
Each element's README lists its values key, settings and Policies: stack/gitops/README.md for gitops (Reading an element's README). On prod-east-1, gitops installs the OpenShift GitOps operator, configures that cluster's own Argo CD instance in openshift-gitops, and adds a console link. That Argo CD is for the cluster's workloads; the hub's Argo CD still runs PolicyStack.

The key is the element's chart name in camelCase under stack (gitops here, userMonitoring for user-monitoring), because Go templates can't read a key containing - with dot syntax (Anatomy). Create the cluster file if it's missing. Its name must match the ManagedCluster exactly, or it is skipped silently:

# values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
stack:
  gitops:
    enabled: true

Enabling enforces at once

Shipped elements default to enforce, so the operator installs as soon as the change syncs. To see what an element would do first, add a dry run to the same file. Every Policy for this cluster then reports only, until you remove it (Dry run):

global:
  remediationAction: inform

Under the dry run expect install NonCompliant (operator not installed) and instance and link Pending, since they wait on install; the Application shows Degraded because some Policies aren't Compliant (Check compliance). Remove the key to enforce (What a dry run can't show).

Turning the element off later deletes its Policies but leaves the operator and Argo CD instance on the cluster (What happens on the managed cluster).

Commit where the cluster reads it. With a branch pin, PR to that branch. With a tag or SHA, merge to main, tag, and move revision in the fleet file. A change reaches only clusters that read the file and pin a revision containing it, so this one reaches only prod-east-1. A shared layer such as environments/prod.yaml reaches every cluster that lists it.

items.title: What you created
items.text:
Application gitops-prod-east-1 renders into pstack:

Object Name From Policy install-gitops-prod-east-1 operatorPolicies.gitops in the element's values: the operator Policy instance-gitops-prod-east-1 converters/instance/: the Argo CD instance and its CA bundle. Waits for install. Policy link-gitops-prod-east-1 converters/link/: the console link. Waits for instance. Placement, PlacementBinding gitops-prod-east-1 Selects the cluster whose name label is prod-east-1

A Policy is named <policy>-<element>-<cluster> (Rendered names). ACM copies each into the hub namespace named after the cluster as pstack.<name>. That copy is what the cluster applies, and where its compliance is reported (How a Policy reaches a cluster).

items.title: Check compliance
items.text:
oc get applications.argoproj.io gitops-prod-east-1 -n openshift-gitops
# NAME                 SYNC STATUS   HEALTH STATUS
# gitops-prod-east-1   Synced        Healthy
oc get policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n prod-east-1
# NAME                                 REMEDIATION ACTION   COMPLIANCE STATE   AGE
# pstack.install-gitops-prod-east-1    enforce              Compliant          3m
# pstack.instance-gitops-prod-east-1   enforce              Compliant          3m
# pstack.link-gitops-prod-east-1       enforce              Compliant          3m

Synced means the Policies on the hub match Git. Health is Argo CD's summary of their compliance: Healthy when every Policy is Compliant, Degraded when one is NonCompliant or Pending, Progressing until ACM reports a status. The ACM console shows the same under Governance. enforce changes the cluster to match; inform only reports (Compliance states).

On the cluster itself:

oc --context prod-east-1 get csv -n openshift-gitops-operator   # PHASE Succeeded
oc --context prod-east-1 get argocd -n openshift-gitops         # the instance
Pending

A Policy waiting on another is Pending. instance waits until install is Compliant, which happens once the operator has installed. link waits for instance. Expect a few minutes. Pending for more than about 10 minutes means install is not Compliant; read its message as below.

NonCompliant

Read each template's last message on the cluster's copy:

oc get policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io pstack.instance-gitops-prod-east-1 -n prod-east-1 \
  -o jsonpath='{range .status.details[*]}{.templateMeta.name}{": "}{.history[0].message}{"\n"}{end}'
Application shows ComparisonError

The render failed, so Argo CD syncs and prunes nothing for that Application (When an Application fails). A misspelled key fails the element's schema:

oc get applications.argoproj.io gitops-prod-east-1 -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[*].message}'
# ... values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
# stack:
# - gitops: Additional property enabeld is not allowed

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
• How an element is built: where Policies and their names come from.
  • Rolling out changes: promote, roll back, remove an element.
  • Building clusters: let the hub build the cluster. Skip the import and add hub, version and install to the fleet file.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
PolicyStack runs on the ACM hub: a Helm release from install/ points the hub's Argo CD at your repository, and ACM delivers the Policies Argo CD renders, hub objects that describe a cluster's configuration (ACM policies in brief, what the release creates).

  • An element is a Helm chart under stack/ that turns settings for one product into Policies. Every element ships off.
  • A layer is a values file under values/ that turns elements on and configures them.
  • A fleet file, fleet/<cluster>.yaml, enrolls one cluster and lists the layers it reads. The hub is itself a managed cluster, enrolled by fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml.

You create your own repository with copier, which copies the framework and each element you want from an upstream release tag vX.Y.Z, and records what it copied. Later, copier update merges a newer release with your changes, for you to open as a PR (Upgrading PolicyStack). Full model: How PolicyStack works.

  1. Check the prerequisites
  2. Create your repository
  3. Add elements
  4. Protect the repository
  5. Install the operators (new hubs only)
  6. Install PolicyStack
  7. Add the hub's fleet file
  8. Hand the operators to PolicyStack (later, once the stack is proven)

Run every command from the root of your repository's clone, logged in to the hub as a cluster administrator.

Placeholder Meaning Example <hub> The hub's name in PolicyStack (hubName). Every hub's own ManagedCluster is called local-cluster, so PolicyStack needs a unique name to pick the hub's files (The hub). Lowercase DNS label, at most 30 characters (Naming limits). hub-east <org>/<repo> Your GitHub org and repository acme/fleet

Choose hubName once

Changing it deletes and recreates the hub's own Applications and Policies, and abandons the clusters this hub built until their fleet files name the new hub (The hub). Two active hubs with one hubName apply the same hub file and build the same clusters.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• An empty Git repository, private or public. Argo CD can read any Git server, but the CI checks, CODEOWNERS and rulesets below are GitHub-specific.
  • copier 9.18 or later, git and Python on your workstation: pipx install copier. Once the repository exists, mise install installs the copier version it pins (Setup).
  • oc, and helm 3.14 or later: upgrades use --reset-then-reuse-values, added in 3.14. You need 3.17 or later only if the install hits an ownership conflict. Your local helm runs only the install chart. Argo CD renders elements with the Helm bundled in GitOps (3.18.4 in 1.18), and CI uses the same version.
  • Supported floors: ACM 2.16, OpenShift 4.20, OpenShift GitOps 1.18 (Support). Cluster lifecycle has extra requirements (Cluster lifecycle prerequisites).
  • The hub manages itself: MultiClusterHub self-management on, the ACM default. It creates the hub's ManagedCluster (local-cluster by default), which carries the local-cluster label. Without it the hub never picks up fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml, gets no Applications and builds no clusters.
  • A hub that already runs OpenShift GitOps must use its default Argo CD instance, openshift-gitops. The install chart creates its objects in that namespace and grants Policy rights to that instance's application controller; another instance has neither.
  • The hub is not a passive DR hub. On a passive DR hub, install PolicyStack only at takeover (Hub disaster recovery).
copier --version                         # copier 9.18.0 or later
helm version --short                     # v3.14.0 or later
oc auth can-i '*' '*' --all-namespaces   # yes
oc get managedclusters -l local-cluster=true
# NAME            HUB ACCEPTED   ...   AVAILABLE
# local-cluster   true           ...   True

The last command applies to a hub that already runs ACM. A new hub creates local-cluster in Install the operators.

items.title: Create your repository
items.text:
Argo CD reads only your repository. Upstream ships no fleet files and no live configuration.

Pick the newest framework release, a tag vX.Y.Z on the releases page, and copy it:

url=https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git
copier copy --vcs-ref v1.0.0 "$url" <repo> # (1)!
cd <repo>
git init -b main && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: PolicyStack v1.0.0"
git remote add origin https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git
git push -u origin main
  1. Without --vcs-ref, copier takes the newest release. Name the release so the copy is the one you picked.

You now have the framework (install/, lifecycle/, lib/, tools/, the CI workflows and hooks, mise.toml, the root values.yaml) and .copier-answers.yml, which records the release you copied:

.copier-answers.yml
# Changes here will be overwritten by Copier; NEVER EDIT MANUALLY
_commit: v1.0.0
_src_path: https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git
element: ''

copier update reads _commit to know what to merge, and the validator reads it to check every fleet pin (POLICY052) and every element's release (POLICY061). Never edit it by hand (Answers files).

copier leaves out stack/, which you fill in the next step, and everything that stays upstream: the docs, the upstream README and CODEOWNERS, and the example values/ files (Example files). Who owns each path from here on: The repository.

items.title: Add elements
items.text:
Each element is copied on its own into stack/<element>/, from the same release tag as the framework, and gets its own .copier-answers.yml. Every repository needs acm, gitops and upgrade: Install the operators reads the first two, and upgrade applies a fleet file's version and channel. Add any others the same way, now or later:

url=https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git
for el in acm gitops upgrade cert-manager; do
  copier copy --vcs-ref v1.0.0 -d element="$el" "$url" "stack/$el" # (1)!
done
git add stack && git commit -m "feat: add acm, gitops, upgrade and cert-manager"
  1. The _commit in your root .copier-answers.yml. An element added later takes that tag too: an element may be older than your framework, never newer. An element that first ships in a newer release needs the framework updated to that release first (Framework updates); until then copier copy fails with FileNotFoundError: ... stack/<element>.

Pass --vcs-ref for every element

Without it copier copies the newest release, which can be newer than your framework. That element may then need framework code you don't have yet, and POLICY061 fails it. Delete the directory and copy it again with your framework's tag.

Each element is either stable or preview, shown at the top of its README.md. A preview element may change incompatibly in a framework minor (Element stability). Each element's settings are in its README.md.

Some elements depend on another: odf, for one, waits on Policies of storage-nodes. Copy both. Once the first fleet file exists, CI fails a missing dependency with POLICY011, naming it. In your repository the validator checks elements and values only through the clusters in fleet/ (What validate runs).

Elements you write yourself also go under stack/, without an answers file (Writing an element).

items.title: Protect the repository
items.text:
1. Protect fleet/. A fleet file decides which revision and layers a cluster reads, and a fleet file with hub: and state: absent makes the hub delete that cluster (Cluster lifecycle). Clusters pinned to a branch also take every merge to values/ and stack/ on that branch, so if production follows main, own those paths too, or pin production to tags (Rolling out changes). Write your own CODEOWNERS:

    # .github/CODEOWNERS
/fleet/ @<org>/<team>

    The team needs write access to the repository. To protect only production, own /fleet/prod-*.yaml and /fleet/hubs/ instead.

  2. Add a ruleset on the default branch (Settings > Rules > Rulesets). Without one nothing blocks a merge:

    • Require a pull request with code owner review.
    • Require the status checks ci and pr-title. The picker lists only checks that have run, so open one PR first (the fleet PR in Add the hub's fleet file works), or type the names.
    • Block force pushes and deletion.

    These checks run on every PR (CI workflows, Validator rules):

    Check What it does for you ci Runs the lint hooks from .pre-commit-config.yaml (a hook that rewrites a file fails and prints the diff) and the validator. The validator renders every fleet cluster the way Argo CD will and checks the result, each fleet file and its revision (POLICY050, POLICY052), and every values key (POLICY035). pr-title The PR title must be a Conventional Commit, such as feat: enable gitops on prod-east-1. Render Diff On PRs to the default branch, comments the Policies each fleet cluster gains, loses or changes. It only reports and never blocks.

Label rights change what clusters run

Anyone who can label ManagedClusters or edit the cluster Secrets in openshift-gitops can switch a cluster to another fleet file. Keep both rights to hub admins (Labels).

items.title: Install the operators
items.text:
New hubHub that already runs ACM and GitOps

Installs ACM and OpenShift GitOps and creates the MultiClusterHub. The chart renders a Namespace, OperatorGroup and Subscription for each operator (ACM on channel release-2.17, GitOps on latest, both with automatic approval) plus the MultiClusterHub. These are the same names and specs the acm and gitops elements enforce, so handover later adopts them in place. helm template | oc apply leaves no Helm release, so after handover only the elements own these objects.

until helm template install/operators -f stack/acm/values.yaml -f stack/gitops/values.yaml \
      | oc apply -f - && oc get argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops; do sleep 30; done

The first passes fail with no matches for kind "MultiClusterHub" until ACM registers its CRD. The loop ends once the GitOps operator has created its default Argo CD instance, openshift-gitops. If it never ends, stop it and read the oc error. The usual cause is an unreachable catalog:

oc get packagemanifest advanced-cluster-management openshift-gitops-operator -n openshift-marketplace

NotFound means the redhat-operators catalog isn't reachable. On a disconnected hub, pass the global.catalogSources layer (below).

Verify. The MultiClusterHub takes about 10 minutes:

oc wait mch/multiclusterhub -n open-cluster-management --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Running --timeout=20m
# multiclusterhub.operator.open-cluster-management.io/multiclusterhub condition met
oc wait argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Available --timeout=10m
# argocd.argoproj.io/openshift-gitops condition met

The chart installs the newest version in each channel. It fails with versions and upgradeApproval pins apply only after handover if the values you pass pin a version, because a plain Subscription with automatic approval can't hold one. Pin after handover (Operator versions).

Single node or disconnected hub

Write a values layer: a YAML file under values/ that the hub's fleet file will list. Settings for the acm element go under stack.acm:

# values/acm/<hub>.yaml
stack:
  acm:
    config:
      availabilityConfig: Basic  # (1)!
  1. Single replicas, for lab and single node hubs. The default is High.

Pass it with -f:

until helm template install/operators -f stack/acm/values.yaml -f stack/gitops/values.yaml \
      -f values/acm/<hub>.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc get argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops; do sleep 30; done

Commit this file and list it in the hub's fleet file. At handover the acm element enforces availabilityConfig on the MultiClusterHub, and without this layer it switches the hub to High.

On a disconnected hub, also pass the layer that sets global.catalogSources, which points each Subscription at your mirrored catalog, such as -f values/datacenters/<dc>.yaml (Disconnected clusters).

Skip this step. Your operators keep running as they are. Run the compatibility checks before enabling the acm or gitops element.

If only one of them runs, install the other from OperatorHub following the Red Hat docs (GitOps: namespace openshift-gitops-operator, channel latest). Don't run this chart: it renders both, and would create a second Subscription for the one already installed.

items.title: Install PolicyStack
items.text:
Private repository: add a repository secret first

Argo CD needs credentials to read a private repo (Argo CD docs). Without them the ApplicationSets can't read the repository and create no Applications.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: policystack-repo
  namespace: openshift-gitops
  labels:
    argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: repository
stringData:
  type: git
  url: https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git
  username: <user>
  password: <token>  # (1)!
  1. A fine-grained personal access token with read-only Contents access to this one repository.

Apply it with oc apply -f -. Never commit it.

helm install policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops \
  --set hubName=<hub> --set gitRepo=https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git

Both values are required and stored in the release; upgrades reuse them. The release's chart version is the framework release it came from, which upgrades compare against. The release creates (Install chart):

Object Why ApplicationSet policystack One Application per element per cluster, named <element>-<cluster>. Each renders the element's Policies into pstack. ApplicationSet policystack-lifecycle One Application per cluster this hub builds. Creates nothing until a fleet file sets hub: <hub> (Cluster lifecycle). Namespace pstack Holds the Policies. GitOpsCluster argo-acm-importer-global, Placement global Create the Argo CD cluster secret for every ManagedCluster (Cluster secrets). ManagedClusterSetBinding global ACM lets a Placement choose only from cluster sets bound into its namespace. global is ACM's built-in set containing every ManagedCluster. Bound in openshift-gitops (for the GitOpsCluster) and pstack (for the element Placements). ClusterRole and binding openshift-gitops-policy-admin Let Argo CD manage Policies, Placements and PlacementBindings.

Verify:

oc get applicationsets -n openshift-gitops
# NAME                    AGE
# policystack             10s
# policystack-lifecycle   10s
oc get secrets -n openshift-gitops -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster
# one secret per ManagedCluster, including the hub

No secret for the hub means it doesn't manage itself (Prerequisites).

... exists and cannot be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata

An object of the same name already exists. Hubs set up with the ACM GitOps guide often have ManagedClusterSetBinding global in openshift-gitops and ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding openshift-gitops-policy-admin. Rerun with --take-ownership (Helm 3.17 or later) to adopt them. Adoption replaces their spec with the chart's.

items.title: Add the hub's fleet file
items.text:
A fleet file enrolls a cluster: Argo CD reads it from the default branch, and it names the revision (branch, tag or SHA) at which stack/ and values/ are read, plus the values layers the cluster gets (Fleet files). The hub reads fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml, never fleet/<cluster>.yaml.

Start with a file that lists no layers:

# fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml
revision: main  # (1)!
  1. A branch the cluster follows, or a tag or SHA it stays on (Revision). Name your default branch if it isn't main.

PR it to the default branch and merge. Within about 6 minutes (the ApplicationSet polls Git every 3 minutes) every directory under stack/ gets an Application named <element>-<hub>, one per element you copied. Each shows Synced and Healthy and renders nothing, because every element ships off except upgrade, which acts only when a fleet file sets version or channel.

oc get applications.argoproj.io -n openshift-gitops | grep <hub>  # (1)!
# acm-<hub>      Synced   Healthy
# gitops-<hub>   Synced   Healthy
# ...
  1. ACM installs a second applications kind, so use the full name.

Then turn elements on through layers. A layer sets stack.<element>.enabled; the key is the element name in camelCase (Enable an element):

# values/environments/hub.yaml
stack:
  certManager:
    enabled: true

List each layer under valueFiles, lowest precedence first (Order). A values/clusters/<hub>.yaml, if you add one, is always read last, without being listed, and holds hub-only settings:

# fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml
revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/hub.yaml  # (1)!
  1. Add acm/<hub>.yaml too if you wrote it under Single node or disconnected hub.

Listed layers apply at once, with enforce

Every shipped element enforces by default, so the hub changes as soon as the PR merges. If you copied a layer from upstream's examples (Example files), read it first: they turn elements on. Or put global.remediationAction: inform in values/clusters/<hub>.yaml to report without changing anything (Dry run).

Every valueFiles entry must exist at the revision. Argo CD skips a missing file silently, but CI fails the PR:

error POLICY050 invalid fleet file: valueFiles "acm/hub-east.yaml": not a file under values/
error POLICY052 revision "main" has no values/acm/hub-east.yaml, which Argo CD skips

Commit the layer in the same PR, or leave the entry out until you need it.

No Applications after 6 minutes

Read the ApplicationSet's error first:

oc get applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="ErrorOccurred")].message}'
Cause Symptom File name differs from hubName, or the file isn't on the default branch No error. Nothing happens. YAML error, no revision, or a revision that doesn't exist Error above. No cluster on this hub gets Application changes until it is fixed (One bad fleet file stops the hub). Private repository without a repository secret Error above: authentication or repository not found. Hub doesn't manage itself No hub cluster secret (Prerequisites).

Check the Policies the hub got and whether they comply. The Policies Argo CD syncs from Git (root Policies) are in pstack. ACM copies each (a replicated Policy) into the namespace of the hub's ManagedCluster, which carries the per-cluster compliance (Check compliance). Both are empty until a layer enables an element:

oc get policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n pstack
oc get policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n local-cluster

Managed clusters follow the same pattern with fleet/<cluster>.yaml (First cluster).

items.title: Hand the operators to PolicyStack
items.text:
Optional. Without it, both operators keep their Subscriptions as installed (Install the operators sets automatic approval, so they upgrade on their own within their channels), and PolicyStack can't pin their versions. Handover enables the acm and gitops elements on the hub. Their install Policy, generated from each element's operatorPolicies (The install Policy), then enforces the operators' Subscription and OperatorGroup: channel, approved versions and upgrades. The acm element's hub Policy enforces the MultiClusterHub.

Wait until the hub's other Applications have stayed Synced and Healthy through a few changes. PolicyStack is delivered by this ACM and this Argo CD, so a bad value in these two elements can break the path that would deliver the fix.

items.title: Existing hub: check compatibility
items.text:
The install Policy's OperatorPolicy (the ACM template that manages a Subscription and OperatorGroup, OperatorPolicy) names its Subscription after the operator package and finds it by namespace and that name. An element adopts an operator only when the namespace, OperatorGroup name and Subscription name match the element.

Warning

A namespace or Subscription name mismatch makes the OperatorPolicy create a second Subscription.

  1. List the operators' Subscriptions, OperatorGroups and the MultiClusterHub:

    oc get subscriptions.operators.coreos.com -A \
  -o custom-columns=NS:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,PACKAGE:.spec.name,CHANNEL:.spec.channel \
  | grep -E 'advanced-cluster-management|openshift-gitops-operator'
oc get operatorgroups -n <NS>   # <NS> from the first command
oc get mch -A

  2. Compare them with the names each element expects:

    Element Namespace OperatorGroup Subscription acm open-cluster-management open-cluster-management advanced-cluster-management gitops openshift-gitops-operator openshift-gitops-operator openshift-gitops-operator

  3. Fix each mismatch in values/acm/<hub>.yaml, the same layer the next step enables both elements in. Short keys in the Fix column are under stack.<element>.operatorPolicies.<element>, for example stack.acm.operatorPolicies.acm.subscription.channel.

    Mismatch Fix NAME differs from PACKAGE Leave that element off. The OperatorPolicy would create a second Subscription for the same package. NS differs, such as GitOps in openshift-operators Set namespace and operatorGroup.name to match, or leave the element off. Otherwise the Policy creates a second Subscription and OperatorGroup in the element's namespace, which OLM refuses to install, and the Policy stays NonCompliant. Console-created OperatorGroup, <ns>-xxxxx Set operatorGroup.name to it. Another name makes the Policy NonCompliant. Older channel Set subscription.channel to it, then move one minor at a time. MultiClusterHub not multiclusterhub in open-cluster-management Leave acm off. The hub Policy manages only that name. MultiClusterHub on Basic Set stack.acm.config.availabilityConfig: Basic, or handover switches it to High.

    For example, GitOps in openshift-operators:

    # values/acm/<hub>.yaml
stack:
  gitops:
    operatorPolicies:
      gitops:
        namespace: openshift-operators
        operatorGroup:
          name: global-operators

items.title: Enable the elements
items.text:
Enable both elements in the hub's layer, and list that layer in fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml in the same PR:

# values/acm/<hub>.yaml
stack:
  acm:
    enabled: true
  gitops:
    enabled: true
    policies:
      instance:
        enabled: false  # (1)!
      link:
        enabled: false  # (2)!
  1. instance and link are the gitops element's other Policies, from converters/instance/ and converters/link/ (Reading an element's README, gitops README). instance manages the Argo CD instance that delivers PolicyStack. Never let PolicyStack reconcile it: a bad value there breaks the path that fixes it.
  2. The console link depends on instance. Left on, it would stay Pending.

Don't rerun Install the operators after handover

oc apply writes the channel and automatic approval from whatever values you pass. The install Policy changes them back, but in between OLM can follow the wrong channel or approve an upgrade past a versions pin.

Verify:

oc get policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n local-cluster | grep -E 'acm|gitops'
# pstack.hub-acm-<hub>          enforce   Compliant
# pstack.install-acm-<hub>      enforce   Compliant
# pstack.install-gitops-<hub>   enforce   Compliant
oc get csv -n open-cluster-management   # the same CSV as before, not a reinstall

All three turn Compliant within a few minutes. NonCompliant on install means a name in the compatibility table doesn't match: read the template's message (Check compliance) and fix the override.

ACM and GitOps upgrades now follow the hub's fleet revision like any other element (Operator versions).

items.title: Teardown
items.text:
oc delete applicationset policystack policystack-lifecycle -n openshift-gitops

This deletes every Application, and each Application deletes the Policies it rendered. ACM then stops applying them, but what they created on the clusters stays, operators included (What happens on the managed cluster). Clusters this hub built keep running, unmanaged (Abandon).

Every other chart object carries helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so helm uninstall removes only the release record. Once oc get policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n pstack returns nothing, remove the rest. Skip any object you created yourself and adopted with --take-ownership:

helm uninstall policystack -n openshift-gitops
oc delete gitopscluster argo-acm-importer-global -n openshift-gitops  # (1)!
oc delete placement global -n openshift-gitops
oc delete managedclustersetbinding global -n openshift-gitops
oc delete clusterrolebinding,clusterrole openshift-gitops-policy-admin
oc delete namespace pstack
  1. ACM then removes the cluster secrets it created, unless another GitOpsCluster selects the same clusters.

--cascade=orphan is not a way to stop

It deletes only the ApplicationSets. The Applications keep syncing from Git, so PolicyStack keeps managing every cluster. Use it to recreate the ApplicationSets without touching the Policies.

Next: First cluster.
